News.title: ‘Female friend’, 70, charged over killing of Brit Karen Carter, 65, stabbed to death in idyllic French village
News.content:
A 70-year-old woman has been charged over the killing of Karen Carter, who died in her French home more than a year ago.

Brit expat Karen, 65, was murdered in the idyllic French village of Trémolat in April last year.



Karen was found slashed to death in what French cops described as a “frenzied attack” in the driveway of her own home last year.

Prosecutors have now revealed that the 70-year-old woman was originally taken into custody in 2025 as part of preliminary inquiries before being released.



The public prosecutor of Périgueux, Jacques-Edouard Andrault, told Sud Ouest: “On July 2nd, the investigating judge in Périgueux formally charged a woman with murder.

“This 70-year-old woman, originally from Trémolat, was taken into custody on April 30, 2025, during a preliminary investigation before being released.

“Since then, the investigations conducted as part of the judicial inquiry opened on May 7, 2025 have led the investigating judge to indict her.”

Karen lived alone in a renovated farmhouse in the French village, east of Bordeaux, and was a popular figure in the village before her death in April 2025.



Her body sustained eight major wounds – to the chest, groin, in the arm and one of her legs.

Emergency services rushed to the scene, but despite their best efforts , she was pronounced dead.

The cause of her death was described as a “massive haemorrhage”.

The Brit was reportedly on the verge of divorcing her husband Alan Carter before her death.

Karen was seeing Jean-François Guerrier, a 75-year-old retired business executive who lived nearby, at the time of her death.



They both have strongly denied any wrongdoing, continuing to cooperate with investigators.

On the day of her murder, Jean-François had hosted a wine-tasting and later followed her home in his car.

When he arrived, he found Karen lying in a pool of blood.

Jean-François told investigators he first suspected something was wrong when Karen did not call him after getting home, which was just a 10-minute drive away.

At the time of the killing, Alan said that he first heard of her death when a cousin contacted him after reading about the death on a local community Facebook page.



He said he received confirmation of the death after his assistant phoned local police.

Describing his wife as an outgoing, friendly person who “wouldn’t hurt a fly”, he said her death has been “traumatic” for his family.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

He said: “I’m an introvert, and she’s the exact opposite. She’s an extrovert, she loves people, she loves to have fun. People love her, she has a good heart.

“She’s the one who would bring home the lost dog, or cat, or whatever. She’s that sort of person. Everyone liked her. That’s why I married her. She’s just lovely.”

News.title: Female colleagues complain of ‘leg hair harassment’ as male workers encouraged to ditch suit for shorts in 40C Tokyo
News.content:
HAIRY SITUATION Female colleagues complain of ‘leg hair harassment’ as male workers encouraged to ditch suit for shorts in 40C Tokyo

FEMALE workers have complained of “leg hair harassment” after their male colleagues were encouraged to wear shorts as temperatures soar.

Disgruntled female office workers in Japan have expressed their irritation as their male counterparts get their legs out as part of a government heatwave health initiative.



While some enjoy the relaxed rules others say the policy is discriminatory.

Traditional Japanese etiquette expects women to still wear tights when their work attire exposes their legs in an office environment.



Many women describe the experience as “leg hair harassment” or “sunehara” as coined online.

Named “Tokyo Cool Biz”, the initiative has become a stalwart in the hotter months in the country’s business capital.



It comes as part of an upgraded version of “Cool Biz”, an energy-saving campaign that encouraged bureaucrats to ditch ties and jackets in summer, started in 2005.

Tokyo Metropolitan Government environmental official Noboru Watanabe told the BBC: “We want to give people more options in the severe heat, not tell them what to wear.



“There should be no issue as long as the work attire is not offensive to anyone.”

A survey conducted in June by Gorilla Clinic revealed 53.5 per cent of people opposed the wearing of shorts to work in summer while 46.5 per cent were in favour.

The results suggested women significantly outnumbered men in their opposition, indicating that women were more resistant to seeing a male colleague’s bare legs.

For all those against shorts in the office the main reason cited was the concern over body shape and body hair.

Sachie Koike, a 52-year-old real estate agent, said she was fine with men ditching a tie or jacket in summer but thinks shorts are a step too far.



She said: “I associate them with a day-off.

“I just don’t think hairy legs look very neat.”

Takayuki Deguchi, a 30-year-old marketing employee says he would love take part in the initiative but his work still insists on suits.

He said: “I think being able to wear shorts that allow you to regulate your temperature when it’s so hot is a very flexible approach.”

The loosening of a strict dress code, particularly for men, comes as Japanese offices cut reliance on air conditioning due to high energy costs linked to the Middle East war.



On Wednesday temperatures in Japan soared past 40C.

The Tokyo Fire Department said a total of 287 people, aged three to 103, were taken to the city’s hospitals on Tuesday because of apparent heatstroke, the BBC reports.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Last year Japan sweltered through its hottest summer since records began in 1898, according to the Japan Meteorological Agency.

Scientists say human-driven climate change is making extreme weather more frequent, prolonged and intense.

﻿

News.title: Russian exec ‘who knew secrets of Putin enemy’s death’ is found hanged on Moscow balcony in another mysterious ‘suicide’
News.content:
A RUSSIAN executive who “knew secret details about the death of a leading Putin foe” has been found dead in another mysterious “suicide”.

VIP airport terminal director Alexey Korshenko, 57, was discovered hanged on his balcony in Moscow.



His body was found on June 6, but details of his death have only now emerged.

His death was officially confirmed as a suicide, but Telegram channel VChK-OGPU reported that Korshenko’s friends believe he was murdered.



Head of Wagner private army, Yevgeny Prigozhin, 62, led a coup against Putin but was killed in a horror mid-air explosion on his private jet in August 2023.

“Korshenko knew the full sequence of events surrounding Prigozhin’s aircraft before the explosion and what had taken place on the day of the crash,” VChK-OGPU , which has close law enforcement links, reported.

Korshenko was the boss of the VIP terminal in St Petersburg, where Prigozhin’s plane departed.

Korshenko had been fired from his executive role shortly before his death, according to Russian media.



He also worked in different senior roles for companies linked to oligarch Gennady Timchenko, a long-time Putin associate.

Prigozhin’s death was widely seen as Putin’s revenge for his former loyalist leading a coup attempt, but the Kremlin has denied any role in his death.

He was known as “Putin’s chef” as he owned several restaurants and catering businesses that provided services to the Kremlin.

Russian secret services were suspected of carrying out the secret killing.

An explosive device was reportedly placed in a replacement air cycle machine fitted to the aircraft shortly before its departure.



The spare part had been swapped with one ordered from the US after the original part was broken in suspicious circumstances.

The replacement part came from Protektor, a company which allegedly has close ties to the Russian Federal Security Service (FSB).

Korshenko had key information surrounding the mysterious explosion of Prigozhin’s aircraft, VChK-OGPU and Rucriminal.info claim.

They added that after his death “those questions may now remain unanswered.”

Among the dead in the plane explosion, was key figure Dmitry Utkin, 53, Wagner’s co-founder and military commander.



A former GRU special-forces officer, and flight attendant Kristina Raspopova, 39, were also among the ten dead.

Dozens of Russian executives have died in mysterious circumstances since before the start of Putin’s war against Ukraine.

In Spetember 2025, the decapitated body of top Russian boss Alexei Sinitsyn, 49, was discovered under a bridge in Kaliningrad, Russia.

Sinitsyn’s death was labelled a suicide by Russian media, before any investigation into his cause of death had begun.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

In March 2023, Sergey Grishin, the so-called “Scarface” oligarch who sold Meghan and Harry their California mansion, died from sepsis after criticising the Russian tyrant.



Russian scientist Andrey Botikov, who created the “Sputnik V” COVID-19 vaccine, was strangled with a belt in his apartment the same month.

News.title: Who supplies my water? How to find your local water supplier by postcode – and whether they have a hosepipe ban
News.content:
MILLIONS of households across the UK are facing hosepipe bans after an exceptionally warm and dry spring.

Major water companies – including Thames Water, Anglian Water, Affinity Water, and Southern Water – have rolled out Temporary Use Bans (TUBs) across large parts of the country to protect dwindling water levels.



With restrictions coming into force, many are wondering who actually supplies their water and whether the ban applies to them.

Unlike gas or electricity, water isn’t a market where you can shop around for a cheaper tariff.



Your property is served by a fixed regional provider that owns the local infrastructure, pipes your fresh water, and manages your wastewater.

Whether you need to check if your hose is off-limits, report a leaking main, or trace who bills your address, finding your provider takes under 60 seconds – using just your postcode.



How to find your local water supplier by postcode

Finding out who supplies your home takes less than a minute.

Because water coverage is fixed by location, your postcode gives you the precise answer right away.

Water UK – the trade body representing UK water companies – runs a simple, free online lookup tool.

Just type in your postcode, and it will reveal the exact company responsible for your home.



The Consumer Council for Water (CCW) also provides a clear directory and lookup tool for households across England, Wales, Scotland, and Northern Ireland.

If you don’t have access to the internet, your physical water bill will clearly name your provider.

If you rent, your tenancy agreement or welcome pack will usually list your account details.

Which water bill should I pay attention to?

In many parts of the UK, one water-only company provides clean drinking water, while a larger, regional firm handles sewerage and wastewater services.

If you receive two separate bills, that is completely normal.



If you do receive two bills for your water, the company enforcing any hosepipe ban will always be your clean water supplier.

Clean water suppliers pump fresh, treated water to your home. Because the bans are designed to preserve freshwater levels, this is the company whose restriction rules you must follow.

Sewerage and wastewater companies do not control or supply the water coming out of your taps, so their announcements regarding hosepipe bans do not apply to your home.

If you’re still unsure which one of your two bills is which, look for items labelled “Water Supply” or “Fresh Water”. The company sending this statement is your clean water provider.

Head to that company’s website and enter your postcode to confirm whether a hosepipe ban is active where you live.



What hosepipe bans are currently in place?

This is a full list of all of the major water suppliers that have declared a hosepipe ban in the UK [correct as of July 22]:

Affinity Water: Active since July 11 (Central region, including parts of Herts, Beds, Bucks, Berks, Surrey, and North/West London).

Active since (Central region, including parts of Herts, Beds, Bucks, Berks, Surrey, and North/West London). Anglian Water: Active since July 11 (Norfolk, Suffolk, Lincolnshire, Cambridgeshire, and East Midlands).

Active since (Norfolk, Suffolk, Lincolnshire, Cambridgeshire, and East Midlands). Cambridge Water: Active since July 17 (Cambridgeshire area).

Active since (Cambridgeshire area). South East Water: Active in Kent since July 3 . Extends to Sussex, Surrey, Hampshire, and Berkshire from 12.01am Saturday, July 25 .

Active in Kent since . Extends to Sussex, Surrey, Hampshire, and Berkshire from . South West Water: Active since July 14 (Mid Devon and parts of East Devon).

Active since (Mid Devon and parts of East Devon). Southern Water: Active since July 10 (Hampshire and Isle of Wight).

Active since (Hampshire and Isle of Wight). Thames Water: Starts 12.01am Thursday, July 23 (London and Thames Valley). Customers are urged to cut use immediately.

Starts (London and Thames Valley). Customers are urged to cut use immediately. Welsh Water: Active since July 19 (Mid and south Ceredigion, north Pembrokeshire, and parts of north Carmarthenshire).

Essex & Suffolk, Severn Trent, and South Staffs Water are currently on conservation warnings asking households to save water voluntarily, though formal bans remain under review.

No restrictions are currently in place for Northumbrian Water, Scottish Water, United Utilities, Wessex Water, and Yorkshire Water.

Where to find your latest hosepipe restriction info

When restrictions are put in place, water companies are legally required to notify the public clearly.



Whenever a ban or severe service issue is active, suppliers almost always display a prominent alert banner at the top of their homepage.

Most supplier sites also feature an interactive map or postcode search box where you can check live service updates, pipe maintenance, and localised alerts.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

If you’re still having trouble, use the search bar on your provider’s site to look up terms like “Water Restrictions” or “Hosepipe Ban”.

Dedicated landing pages should detail exactly what rules are currently enforced in your area.

News.title: Girl, 16, reveals how she watched her pals die in front of her as they lay trapped in car in water-filled ditch for 3hrs
News.content:
NARROW ESCAPE Girl, 16, reveals how she watched her pals die in front of her as they lay trapped in car in water-filled ditch for 3hrs

A TEEN girl has revealed how she watched her friends die as they lay trapped in a car in a water-filled ditch for three hours.

Adam Dudzinski, 17, and his girlfriend Chloe-Ann Naylor, 16, drowned after he lost control of a blue Ford Fiesta while driving in Iwade, Kent.



Kent and Medway Coroner’s Court was told how another 16-year-old spent three hours in the vehicle, which landed upside down in a drainage ditch full of water.

The girl, who cannot be named for legal reasons, was eventually found by her dad, who tracked her location on the Live 360 mobile phone app.



She said Adam had been driving fast but was not speeding and although he tried to slow down, he did not brake in time for the bend.

This caused the vehicle to veer off the road, flip upside down and land in the ditch during the January 3 tragedy.



She explained how she was preparing herself to drown but said Chloe tapping her on the leg “gave her courage” to undo her seatbelt.

While trapped, Adam had said “I am sorry, I am so sorry”, as Chloe tried to keep his head above the water.



The schoolgirl said she kept shouting her friend’s name, but after a time, Chloe tragically stopped answering.

Coroner Ian Potter heard how Sainsbury’s shop worker Adam was driving the two girls to Chloe’s home when tragedy struck.

Adam, who didn’t have a licence and was uninsured, was driving along the dark and remote country road when he lost control at a sharp bend.

Chloe tried to call the emergency services and her mum while she was upside down and trapped but the calls did not connect.

Their worried families reported them missing but there were no clues where they might be.



The 16-year-old girl’s dad then managed to find his daughter even though the 360 app stopped sending coordinates.

He had gone to where its final co-ordinates were registered and discovered the partly submerged vehicle.

After he raised the alarm, paramedics, fire crews, police and the coastguard went to the scene.

Tragically, Chloe and Adam had died by the time they arrived, the inquest heard.

The 16-year-old survivor was taken to hospital but later discharged.



Investigators found no evidence that Adam had been speeding at the time, but he was likely to have been going too fast for the conditions.

Officers tried to press charges against his legal guardian for permitting unlicensed and uninsured driving but the Crown Prosecution Service said there was not enough evidence.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

The coroner concluded the inquest by saying he “was so sorry” for the families’ loss.

Recording accidental death verdicts, he said: “This is a very tragic state of circumstances and I cannot begin to imagine what the three families have been through.”

News.title: Face of superstar actor is emblazoned on supermarket lettuce in VERY unsettling marketing ploy
News.content:
LETTUCE HAVE A LOOK Face of superstar actor is emblazoned on supermarket lettuce in VERY unsettling marketing ploy

THE unsettling face of a beloved Japanese actor has been emblazoned across 10,000 supermarket lettuces in a bizarre marketing ploy.

Thousands of shoppers have been left shocked by the unique packaging surrounding the vegetables which show a frowning TV and film star.



Tatsuya Fujiwara, who is best known for leading roles as Shuya Nanahara in the Battle Royale films and Light Yagami in the Death Note films, is the new lettuce posterboy in Japan.

The 44-year-old has agreed to collaborate with Ajinomoto and JA Zen-Noh Nagano in the Nagano Prefecture – Japan‘s largest domestic lettuce producer.



He is the new face of their “Cook Do Oyster Sauce: Tatsuya Fujiwara’s ‘Buy It Now Lettuce'” campaign.

Several supermarkets in the greater Tokyo area and Kansai region have jumped on the initiative and are selling lettuce sold in eye-catching packaging.



And the idea isn’t just based around increasing sales for JA Zen-Noh Nagano, who already account for approximately 60 per cent of Japan’s domestic lettuce production betweensummer ando autumn.

They are attempting to teach Japanese people about the rising concerns over food waste – particularly in vegetables.



Ajinomoto released shocking statistics revealing more than 60 per cent of people have thrown away lettuce at home because they couldn’t finish it.

President and CEO Shigeo Nakamura said: “We don’t know how to eat it other than in a raw salad, so we can’t use up a whole head.”

Their “Survey on Cooking and Lettuce Consumption in Summer” sparked serious questions over how to change the perception around lettuce waste.

Fujiwara’s face is only one part of the plan with Ajinomoto also sharing a QR code on the back of the packages to allow people to view fresh recipes.

The “Lettuce Instant Disappearance Recipe” is a new website put together by veggie fans to help them use up the greens in a variety of ways.



Some of the meals include chilled rice porridge with shredded lettuce, lettuce dumplings and the strange “instantly disappearing lettuce”.

The promotional packaging started on July 21 and will continue on until stocks run out.

Describing how he was approached for the lettuce marketing scheme, Fujiwara said he was told by Ajinomoto that “lettuce is in crisis”.



They then asked if he would lend his face to a new advert to which he happily said yes.

Hiroshi Kobayashi, the General Manager of the Production and Sales Department at JA Zen-Noh Nagano, said: “When I first heard about the concept for this project, I was honestly very surprised that Tatsuya Fujiwara would be cooperating with us.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“I hope that this eye-catching packaging will encourage many people to enjoy new recipes and fully appreciate the appeal of Nagano Prefecture lettuce.

“I sincerely hope that this initiative will encourage everyone to enjoy eating lettuce deliciously and completely, and that it will lead to a reduction in food waste at home.”

News.title: Moment speeding driver SHRIEKS in terror and begs ‘please help me’ as he’s chased down by police dog
News.content:
THIS is the moment a speeding driver who fled cops before being tracked down by a dog begs “please help me!”

Godfrey Forster-Davies ran from officers but was found thanks to the persistence of police dog Yolo.



The dramatic footage shows the 26-year-old shrieking in terror after being finally caught – and has now admitted driving offences in court.

He ran from police following the incident in Bolsover, Derbyshire, at just after 2.25am on June 18.



PC Matthew Cooling from our roads policing unit saw a man driving a Ford Fiesta with a broken licence plate light.

The driver failed to stop for the officer, reaching speeds of more than 80mph through 30 and 40mph zones, failing to give way at junctions and driving on the wrong side of the road in a pursuit across Bolsover, Shuttlewood and Clowne.

Forster-Davies ran from officers but was quickly tracked down and detained by police dog Yolo and his handler PC Andy Shaw.

He appeared at Chesterfield Magistrates’ Court on July 9 and pleaded guilty to dangerous driving, driving without insurance, failing to stop when required by a constable and driving a vehicle with a tyre which had the ply or cord exposed.



He will be sentenced at the same court on August 27.

News.title: Shoot a ship & we’ll obliterate a power plant, Trump warns Iran as he prepares to blitz ‘impenetrable’ Pickaxe nuke lair
News.content:
DONALD Trump has vowed to obliterate Iranian bridges and power plants for every ship its bloodhounds shoot at in the Strait of Hormuz.

The US president is also gearing up to strike the regime’s Pickaxe Mountain, a fortified underground complex the mullahs are believed to be using as a nuclear lair.



American bombers blitzed the Islamic State for the 11th consecutive night yesterday to grind down its capacity to target vessels passing through the waterway.

Trump followed another ruthless night of bombing by threatening to destroy Iran‘s civilian infrastructure if it continues its brazen attacks.



He wrote on Truth Social: “Any time Iran shoots at a ship in the Strait of Hormuz, whether it be by Missile, Rocket, Drone, or any other weapon, the United States will bomb and destroy ONE BRIDGE OR POWER PLANT.”

The bloodthirsty IRGC has been wreaking havoc in the key shipping lane, through which around a fifth of the world’s oil passes, before the outbreak of the war.



The warring nations temporarily brokered a ceasefire, with Trump signing a memorandum of understanding (MOU) on June 17 and reopening the key trade route.

But on July 7, Iran badly damaged a Qatari liquefied natural gas tanker and another British vessel.



The attack prompted Trump to restart his bombing campaign.

Dozens of strategic port sites were struck, as well operation centres, aircraft hangars, drone facilities and military infrastructure.

After last night’s strikes, US Central Command announced that it was further degrading “Iran’s ability to threaten commercial shipping in the Strait of Hormuz”.



It added that 30 vessels had been targeted in the international waterway over the past three months, endangering “hundreds of innocent mariners and undermined freedom of navigation”.

Trump is continuing to deploy more planes to the region, including extra F-16 and F-35 fighter jets from European bases, a sign the conflict is about to escalate.

As the peace deal was falling apart last week, he received a briefing from ­military chiefs on options to intensify the war.

His sights now appear to be set on the elusive Pickaxe Mountain in the Natanz area, where the regime is thought to have stowed its nuclear material.

“We’ll be hitting that area very probably pretty soon, and there’s not a not a thing they can do about it,” the US President told reporters in the White House.



Asked whether he believes they’ve hidden their nuclear stockpile there, he said: “I think that they may have. We don’t have it on record.

“[But] it doesn’t mean anything unless they have the material.”

Pickaxe is a peak in the mountains surrounding the city of Natanz, and is over 5,000ft high – taller than any mountain in the UK.

Buried 328ft down, the site is heavily fortified, and it is believed that it hosts two tunnel complexes.

The US attacked three Iranian nuclear sites – Fordow, Natanz and Isfahan – deploying 30,000-pound GBU-57 “massive ordnance penetrator” bombs in an operation called “Midnight Hammer” that took place in June 2025.



Trump hailed the strikes as “historically successful” at the time, and just this week he repeated again that Iran would have already unleashed a nuclear weapon on Israel had it not been for the US action during the 12-Day war.

But destroying Pickaxe Mountain will take far more to reach the deeper tunnels.

Experts assess it as being beyond the reach of the most powerful bunker buster bombs in the US arsenal.

Trump’s threat about strikes on the fortress comes after he said that the regime wants to “desperately” meet because they are getting “decimated” – but that he has no interest right now.

Giving a dim view on possible talks to end the war, he said: “Until they are ready to meet in a meaningful way, we have no interest in meeting.”



The US has already deployed extra F-16 and F-35 fighter jets from bases in Europe, as well as aerial refuelling tankers, in a sign the conflict is about to escalate.

The president also received a briefing from ­military chiefs on options to intensify the attacks.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Options include capturing Kharg Island, where 90 per cent of Iranian oil exports pass through and bombing nuclear facilities.

At least three US soldiers have been killed in the renewed fighting, and Trump has ordered the Pentagon to make the regime pay “many times over” for every death.

News.title: Donald Trump threatens to blow up 'bridge or power plant' every time Iran hits ship
News.content:
Donald Trump threatens to blow up 'bridge or power plant' every time Iran hits ship

US President Donald Trump has thrashed out plans for Iran ground invasion as he warned Tehran he will blow up a bridge or a power depot every time they hit a ship in the Strait of Hormuz

View 3 Images Donald Trump speaks during a reception with FIFA President Gianni Infantino last week (Image: AP Photo/Jacquelyn Martin)

US President Donald Trump has threatened to blow up a power plant or bridge every time Iran hits a ship in the latest Middle East crisis escalation.

‌



It came as it emerged Pentagon war-planners are drafting a scheme for a partial ground invasion of Iran if the Tehran regime refuses to back down. The President has not green-lighted a ground assault on key Kharg Island but it is one of the options for escalation with which he has been presented.

‌



Mr Trump stormed: "From this point forward, any time the Islamic Republic of Iran shoots at a ship in the Strait of Hormuz, whether it be by missile, rocket, drone, or any other device or weapon, the United States will bomb and destroy one bridge or power plant, including those located next to, or in, the Capital City of Tehran."

‌



In recent weeks, the Republican leader has made repeated threats against civilian infrastructure as he became frustrated with Iran’s defiance.

Zelensky fires Ukraine's military chief after widespread protests READ MORE :

View 3 Images A plane being prepared for war (Image: X)

But Iran has hit back with warnings of their own escalation, claiming they could attack US bases and even kidnap US soldiers, whisking them back to Tehran. And Tehran’s military even threatened that it America does occupy Khark Island then Iran would go ahead and bomb its own territory. Former Iranian Foreign Minister Manouchehr Mottaki, now a member of parliament, said Iran should go further than striking US bases in the region and consider capturing American soldiers.

‌



He stormed: "The US threats have intensified, and it has said that it will seize Kharg Island and take control of Iran's oil facilities. I have been advocating for a ground war for a long time. We should seize one of the US bases in the region, capture its forces, and bring them back to our country.’ An Iranian army spokesperson warned Iran would bomb its own territory rather than allow US forces to occupy it, as threats of a ground operation grown.

Brigadier General Mohammad Akrami-Nia said on Iranian state television: “If America occupies our territory, we will even bomb our own territory. This is the logic of war." The remarks came as US Central Command marked the tenth consecutive day of strikes against Iranian targets. US President Donald Trump is expected to decide in the coming days how to proceed, with the prospect of a US ground operation or seizure of Iranian territory now openly discussed.The Pentagon is preparing options for ground operations in Iran that would fall short of a full invasion but could involve thousands of troops and take weeks or months.

View 3 Images Bridge hit by US in Iran strikes (Image: ISNA/AFP via Getty Images)

Article continues below

The White House said the Pentagon was working to give the president "maximum optionality" but that "this does not mean the president has made a decision." Iranian MP Ahmad Bakhshayesh Ardestani, a former member of the parliamentary National Security Commission, said Tehran could launch ground attacks on Kuwait and Bahrain if the US invaded Iranian territory. On the prospect of a US assault on Kharg Island, he said Washington might take it for a day but could not hold it. He said: "Iranian missiles from Semnan, Zahedan, Isfahan and elsewhere can reach it. Occupying Kharg Island would turn it into a target for Iran.”

And it is possible Iran could make a bold move to take territory, including the taking of Bubiyan Island which is owned by Kuwait. The island, with an area of 700 square mikles, is Kuwait's largest and sits at the northern end of the Persian Gulf close to Iraq. Some Iranian political figures and social media accounts have considered the scenario in response to a potential US seizure of Kharg, suggesting the IRGC could use regional proxies and its Saberin special forces unit to launch a ground operation through southern Iraq if Washington moved on Iranian territory.

The Saberin unit is an elite IRGC formation with extensive combat experience across Iran and neighbouring countries. Reports of Iranian military movements toward the Kuwaiti border have circulated online. Kuwait hosts US forces and has been among the most heavily targeted countries in the latest wave of Iranian strikes. Earlier reports in March and May alleged that IRGC commandos had targeted Bubiyan and engaged against Kuwaiti forces.

News.title: Donald Trump keeps threatening to commit war crimes as he rapidly unravels over Iran
News.content:
Donald Trump keeps threatening to commit war crimes as he rapidly unravels over Iran

Trump's Middle East adventure was brought into focus in the most acute way, as he travelled to Dover Air Force Base for the dignified transfer of three troops killed in his deepening quagmire - here's what you need to know

View Image Trump travelled to Dover Air Force Base for the dignified transfer of troops killed in his war (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

Donald Trump keeps threatening to commit war crimes, as he rapidly unravels over the Iran war.

‌



The US President is under mounting pressure over the deepening quagmire - and it's starting to show.

‌



He had a minor Oval Office meltdown yesterday, after he was asked what the plan was, given Iran clearly aren't as eager to make a deal as he claims they are.

‌



Today the deep failings of his Middle East adventure were brought into focus in the most acute way, as he travelled to Dover Air Force Base for the dignified transfer of three troops killed by Iran in Jordan and Iraq over the weekend.

And with the midterm elections just months away, Trump's "secretary of War" Pete Hegseth has been forced to acknowledge the eye-watering cost of the war in a Senate committee, for the whole world to see.

Trump is probably committing war crimes already, but will never be prosecuted

Trump turned to Truth Social this morning, threatening to have the US armed forces commit war crimes in Iran on his behalf.

‌



International humanitarian law prohibits the targeting of civilian infrastructure - like bridges, water treatment plants and power stations - unless they can be shown to be in use by the military. And retaliation isn't an excuse.

Nevertheless, Trump posted: "From this point forward, any time the Islamic Republic of Iran shoots at a ship in the Strait of Hormuz, whether it be by Missile, Rocket, Drone, or any other device or weapon, the United States will bomb and destroy ONE BRIDGE OR POWER PLANT, including those located next to, or in, the Capital City of Tehran."

Even threats to destroy infrastructure essential to the civilian population could be considered a war crime.

‌



The thing is, there really isn't a mechanism to prosecute anyone in the Administration for war crimes. The US is not a full signatory to the International Criminal Court. A UN Security Council slap down would be vetoed. And since a 2024 Supreme Court decision, the President has absolute immunity from prosecution within the United States for actions relating to core Presidential powers.

Hegseth revealed the eye watering cost of the war - and asked for more

Pete Hegseth, Trump's "Secretary of War" got an extremely rough ride at a Senate committee yesterday. Like Oliver Twist with a perm-tan, he rocked up at the hearing to make the case for his part of a $95 billion Republican budget package to fund the military, along with aid to farmers and voting law changes that are top White House priorities.

And he admitted the war in Iran had already cost a frankly incomprehensible $37.5 billion.

‌



He said troop training and pay would be in doubt if the military doesn't get more cash. Some $46 billion is required for munitions and expanding production lines, while $21 billion would be for military pay, fuel and replacing equipment.

"Without these funds, we face critical shortfalls that threaten our ability to also simply pay our service members," Hegseth said.

Democrats on the committee pointed out there were still tens of billions of dollars in Pentagon coffers that he asked for last year that have yet to be spent.

‌



He got a pretty rough ride from Senators

John Ossoff, the Junior Democrat from Georgia, was particularly foreinsic in his questioning of Hegseth, much to the Defence Secretary's apparent frustration.

He repeatedly asked Hegseth about his previous statements, in the early weeks of the war, in which he claimed Iran's military had been completely destroyed and rendered "combat ineffective".

Hegseth's answers were evasive, mainly because it's hard to answer a question like that without explaining why, if Iran has no military capabilities left, they keep managing to kill American service personnel.

‌



Content cannot be displayed without consent

Then Senator Gary Peters from Michigan landed the rhetorical blow: "The strait of Hormuz is still closed...it was open before the war. Prices were lower for everybody until the war, and it still remains closed - and tragically our warfighters who everybody cares about are still dying."

Hegseth lashed out at Peters, telling him his characterisation of the war as a failure was "reckless" and "irresponsible", and "smears the sacrifice" of troops involved in the conflict.

‌



Peters pointed out his assessment of the failure was not on the part of the troops, but of their leaders.

"You, sir, are the failure," he said.

Content cannot be displayed without consent

‌



Trump keeps shrugging off the human cost

Trump this morning visited Dover Air Force Base, where a plane arrived carrying the coffins of the three US service personnel killed in his war this weekend.

Of course, while Trump makes a show of honouring the sacrifice of the people he keeps putting in harm's way, he spent a lot of the last 24 hours blaming other people for their deaths.

In his Oval Office Q&A yesterday, he obliquely suggested it was the fault of "other operators" being responsible for protecting the personnel.

‌



"They did slip something through in Jordan," he said. "If we had other operators, you know, it would have not happened, unfortunately."

He went on: "We've stopped almost everything, but when you let other people do your job with the United States - we let other people do the job - and sometimes it doesn't work out so well."

Trump did not elaborate on his comments, and it was not immediately clear who Trump was saying was responsible for protecting US forces in Jordan.

Article continues below

And later on Truth Social, he rolled out a frequent deflection - listing a string of other conflicts America had been involved in for years and the number of casualties in each one. Which is just the kind of whataboutery a grieving family wants to hear from the Commander in Chief.

News.title: Mum tried to donate blood but was told she had low iron levels - they were really sign of cancer
News.content:
Mum tried to donate blood but was told she had low iron levels - they were really sign of cancer

Laura Jackson, 39, said she did not have many symptoms of bowel cancer - including blood in her stool - and had put down her tiredness to being a working mother

View 7 Images Laura Jackson put her tiredness down to working (Image: Laura Jackson / SWNS)

A mum was diagnosed with stage-three bowel cancer after her low iron levels were flagged as she tried to donate blood.

‌



Laura Jackson's GP wanted to investigate further after being concerned by her low iron levels. Two positive FIT tests meant she was referred for a colonoscopy and gastroscopy in May 2025.

‌



Other than tiredness, which she put down to being a "working put, Laura said she had not been experiencing any of the typical symptoms like blood in her stool - but did have infrequent bouts of diarrhoea up to three times in the year leading up to her referral. Doctors later found a 5cm tumour in her large intestine and confirmed she had bowel cancer, which left her needing a third of her bowel removed in a three-hour surgery in July 2025.

‌



View 7 Images Laura was referred for further tests by her GP (Image: Laura Jackson / SWNS)

After her tumour was biopsied, due to the cancer showing deposits in her veins and making attempts to spread, her diagnosis was upped from stage two to three. Six weeks following her surgery in August 2025 Laura underwent four rounds of "mop up" chemotherapy for 12 weeks.

Now, she has no evidence of disease but will be under surveillance for the next five years. Laura, 39, from Southampton, Hampshire, said: "Everything kind of felt a bit surreal in that moment when the doctor told me I had a tumour.

‌



View 7 Images Laura said it felt surreal when she was told about the tumour (Image: Laura Jackson / SWNS)

"The first thing I thought was 'am I going to die?' I thought 'oh my gosh I've got two babies at home, I've got to be there for them'.

"My husband was there with me trying to stay strong but he was crying as well. I don't want to scaremonger but to raise awareness of the FIT test.

‌



"It would have been left and would have spread if I’d not had it done. James van der Beek and Mel from MAFS died of bowel cancer and they were young people.

"I won't be the only person with no symptoms that has advanced cancer." The mum-of-two was heading to donate her rare A-negative blood in April 2025 when she was rejected at an initial screening due to low iron levels.

View 7 Images Laura had about a third of her bowel removed (Image: Laura Jackson / SWNS)

‌



Two positive FIT tests saw her referred to a gastroenterologist for an investigative colonoscopy and gastroscopy. "In that time the only thing I really felt was tiredness," Laura says. I was a working mum, only 38 and had a one and three-year-old that were still up in the night.

"Any tiredness I just disregarded. I never thought, 'oh this is cancer' or that it was anything serious.

"The doctor said my FIT test results were really high and he was expecting to find something, but he didn't expect it to be cancer. When my husband arrived after my procedures the doctor came in with two nurses.

‌



"I said 'oh this isn't good news' trying to crack a joke. Nobody smiled. He said there was nothing in your stomach and your endoscopy was fine, but we found a tumour in your large intestine. It was just the most surreal out of body experience ever."

The next day, Laura had a CT scan to determine what stage her cancer was at and then underwent bowel resection surgery on July 3, 2025.

View 7 Images Laura said she wished she had listened to her body more (Image: Laura Jackson / SWNS)

‌



She says the pain she experienced after surgery was "up there with childbirth" but made it her "mission" in recovery to build up her physical fitness – walking 10,000 steps a day just two weeks later.

She says she wished she had "listened to her body more" when it came to her tiredness, often taking two-hour naps during the day whilst her baby slept. Six weeks after surgery, her cancer was upped to stage three after deposits were found in her veins and outside her bowel.

"When it's upgraded from stage two to three you need to do what they call 'mop up' chemo," she said. The thought of surgery didn't scare me, but chemo did.

‌



"I tried to reframe it in my head that rather than chemo being the scary enemy, chemo was stopping this coming back. I had bad days but other days I felt better and I could go to the gym, go swimming or for family days out."

View 7 Images Laura said she was in a lot of pain following her surgery (Image: Laura Jackson / SWNS)

Laura iced her hands and feet during her chemotherapy to help avoid any long-term neuropathy – nerve damage which can sometimes be induced by chemotherapy leading to symptoms like tingling, numbness, pain and weakness often in the hands and feet.

‌



She says other than tiredness, the one symptom she "completely disregarded" were sudden bouts of diarrhoea. "Three times a year I'd have stomach cramps and need for a number two but nothing was happening," she said.

"The pain was so intense and eventually I'd have frequent diarrhoea. Looking back I had a partial bowel obstruction so my body was having a meltdown trying to pass a bowel motion but the tumour was in the way.

View 7 Images Laura Jackson, pictured with her husband, said she wanted to share her experience to raise awareness (Image: Laura Jackson / SWNS)

‌



"If that was happening every month I'd think 'that's odd and go to the GP but because it didn't I just thought it was one of those things."

After her 12-week treatment, Laura has been recovering and now shows no evidence of disease but will be under surveillance for five years before she can be classed as in remission.

Sharing her story online, Laura says her videos have encouraged other to seek out FIT tests. "My GP saved my life," she says. "I've shared for awareness.

Article continues below

"I thought if I share my experience and someone else is going through it they might be able to see the reality is not all doom and gloom." You can follow Laura on TikTok @‌itslauraunfiltered.

News.title: Heartbreaking last words of teenager to girlfriend after their horror Ford Fiesta crash
News.content:
Heartbreaking last words of teenager to girlfriend after their horror Ford Fiesta crash

Adam Dudzinski, 17, and his girlfriend Chloe-Ann Naylor, 16, drowned after he lost control of a blue Ford Fiesta in Kent and it ended up in a drainage ditch full of water

View 3 Images Adam Dudzinski did not have a driver's licence, it was heard (Image: Cover Images)

A tragic teenager told his girlfriend "I am sorry, I am so sorry" minutes before they died following a horror car crash.

‌



Adam Dudzinski, 17, apologised to 16-year-old Chloe-Ann Naylor after he lost control of the blue Ford Fiesta along a country road. An inquest into their deaths this week heard the vehicle landed upside down in a drainage ditch full of water following the impact near Sittingbourne, Kent.

‌



The hearing was told Adam said "I am sorry, I am so sorry," as Chloe tried to keep his head above water. However, they both drowned while a third teenager, who cannot be named for legal reasons, escaped with significant injuries. Her dad used the Live 360 mobile phone app, which allows people to track each other's locations, to find her.

‌



'Lovely' mum collapses and dies in GP surgery after waiting days for appointment READ MORE :

View 3 Images Chloe-Ann tragically died in the crash (Image: Cover Images)

Although it stopped sending information, he went to where the final co-ordinates were registered and discovered the partly submerged vehicle just before midnight on January 3. Coroner Ian Potter heard this week how Sainsbury's worker Adam was driving the two girls to Chloe's home in Sittingbourne when the crash happened.

The three of them had been at his house, also in the town. Adam, who did not have a licence and was uninsured, was driving along the dark remote country road when he lost control at a sharp bend.

‌



Upside down and trapped, Chloe tried to call the emergency services and her mum, but the calls did not connect. The worried families reported the teenagers missing, but there were no clues where they might be.

After the father of the second girl raised the alarm, paramedics, fire crews, police and the coastguard went to the scene. Tragically, Chloe and Adam had died by the time they arrived after drowning in the water.

Chloe's friend, who had been sitting in the back seat, was taken to hospital and was later discharged. In her police statement, she said Adam had been driving fast but was not speeding, and although he had tried to slow down, he did not brake in time for the bend.

‌



View 3 Images Tributes had been paid to the pair (Image: Cover Images)

This caused the vehicle to veer off the road, flip upside down and land in the ditch. She explained how she was preparing herself to drown and described how Chloe tapping her on the leg "gave her courage" to undo her seat belt.

It was during the time they were trapped that Adam said he was sorry. The schoolgirl kept shouting her friend's name, but after a time, Chloe stopped answering.

‌



Investigators found no evidence that Adam had been speeding at the time, but he was likely to have been going too fast for the conditions.

Officers tried to press charges against his legal guardian for permitting unlicensed and uninsured driving. However, the Crown Prosecution Service said there was not enough evidence to pursue this.

In the days following Chloe's and Adam's deaths, floral tributes were left at the scene. And more than £15,000 was raised in two GoFundMe fundraisers for Chloe and Adam's families.

Article continues below

Click here to view Chloe's page and here for Adam's. The coroner concluded the inquest by saying he "was so sorry" for the families' loss.

Recording accidental death verdicts, he said: "This is a very tragic state of circumstances and I cannot begin to imagine what the three families have been through."

News.title: 'I'm a single mum and often go without the basics - every month is a struggle'
News.content:
'I'm a single mum and often go without the basics - every month is a struggle'

EXCLUSIVE: Lowri Williams relies on Universal Credit and often goes without the basics - it comes as research found 7.4 million households were unable to afford at least one essential in the last month

View 4 Images Lowri's late dad Elwyn helped out with her mortgage payments (Image: Family handout)

A single mum has told how she’s often forced to choose between buying petrol and essential food items.

‌



Lowri Williams, 56, relies on Universal Credit after losing her business in 2017 and regularly goes without the basics. Her elderly father used to help out with the mortgage and food costs, but recently passed away. She told the Mirror: “We have lived day to day for around nine years. We have to judge, depending on what money is or isn’t available, when to buy toiletries, food and petrol.

‌



“It’s often – can we last another week without buying a certain food item and toiletries, or is that £10 better spent on fuel? Every month is a struggle – the mortgage is £650, gas and electric £250, water £100, council tax £150, house and car insurance £120, and that before you even think of food or petrol – it’s a huge strain.”

‌



View 4 Images Some 7.4 million families went without at least one basic household item last month (Image: Jason Roberts /Manchester Evening News)

Lowri, who lives in Blackpool, Lancashire, with her 16-year-old daughter, added: “I feel like I have not lived for nine years. I feel like I have been held back, crushed, made to feel worthless, but the worst part is that my daughter has had to go without things.”

She spoke after new research from the Joseph Rowntree Foundation found a staggering 7.4 million low-income households were unable to afford at least one essential item in the last month. Along with skipping meals, the survey found many families are going without showers and basic toiletries like toothbrushes and sanitary products. Some can’t afford shampoo, soap, prescriptions, pain relief and weather-appropriate clothes and shoes. And others are unable to replace basic household appliances, like washing machines and fridges when they break.

‌



Another single mum on Universal Credit told how she’s had to make huge cut backs despite having a full time job in finance. The 34-year-old, who lives in Sheffield with her son, 11, said: “I’ve worked in finance for three years, but because of the rise in the cost of living, my wages haven’t kept up. I’ve had three promotions, but only one came with a pay rise, which leaves me on only just above minimum wage.

View 4 Images Andy Burnham has promised to put cost of living (Image: Toby Melville/Pool Reuters via A)

“I feel like I’ve made every cut back possible – we’ve swapped fresh food for frozen and I try to do meals as cheaply as I can. We don’t buy much meat anymore because of the expense which worries me as I’ve got a growing boy and he needs a varied diet. We’ve also gone back to sharing bath water, which is something I never thought I’d have to do, and in the winter I can’t have the heating on during the day. It’s really stressful and really worrying.”

‌



New Prime Minister Andy Burnham has promised to put cost of living “front and centre” of his government to provide “breathing space” for households. The Joseph Rowntree Foundation says their findings show both the scale of the issue and the potential for rapid progress with bold policy choices.

The charity’s chief economist Chris Belfield said: “Andy Burnham starts his time as prime minister at a time when the cost-of-living crisis has never been more widely felt. This ongoing crisis is not numbers in a spreadsheet, it is not graphs trending up or down, it is families not being able to afford basic essential goods like food, heating and basic toiletries. We need greater intervention to control rental prices, make energy affordable and improve the adequacy of Universal Credit so everyone can afford the essentials.”

View 4 Images The Joseph Rowntree Foundation's Chris Belfield is calling for more government intervention

‌



Professor Ruth Patrick of Changing Realities, a collaboration of more than 200 parents and carers living on a low income, researchers from the university of Glasgow and LSHTM and Child Poverty Action Group, said: "It is great to see Burnham promise that his will be a ‘cost of living government’, which provides some vital, and urgently needed ‘breathing space’ to struggling households.

"But if he is to deliver on this promise, he needs to be much bolder. Small reduces to electricity bills, and bus fares, are welcome, but - on their own - they simply won’t shift the dial on the pressure cooker of stress, anxiety and financial hardship that millions of families across the UK are facing day in and day out. On Changing Realities, we know that making a real difference also requires working in partnership with and actively listening to those at the sharpest end of the crisis, and Burnham has a time-limited opportunity to do exactly that."

Helen Barnard, director of policy and research at Trussell, added: “The findings from Joseph Rowntree Foundation reflect the reality we see at food banks every day – parents skipping meals to feed their children, people sitting in the dark because they can’t afford to switch on the lights. They are a stark reminder that the cost of living crisis is far from over.

Article continues below

"Too many families across the UK are struggling to afford the essentials like food and toiletries – and alarmingly, hardship is affecting people who had previously been getting by. That should be a massive wake-up call for all of us..The UK Government was elected on a manifesto commitment to end the need for food banks and making this a reality will require targeted support for people who are most at risk of being pulled into hunger and hardship. That includes lifting the freeze on Local Housing Allowance for private renters, and taking steps towards an Essentials Guarantee, so that the basic rate of Universal Credit covers the cost of essentials – like food and toiletries.”

News.title: Police officer charged over death of 16-year-old 10 months after e-bike crash
News.content:
Police officer charged over death of 16-year-old 10 months after e-bike crash

Daniel Cartwright, 31, a serving police officer with Bedfordshire Police, was off duty at the time of the crash between two cars and an e-bike, which resulted in the death of 16-year-old Ryley Hutson

View 2 Images Tributes to 16-year-old Ryley Hutson, who was pronounced dead at the scene on Chilwell Lane in Bramcote (Image: Joseph Raynor/Reach PLC)

A serving police officer is to appear in court charged with causing death by dangerous driving 10 months after a 16-year-old boy was killed while riding an e-bike.

Daniel Cartwright, 31, was off duty at the time of the crash, at 10.10am on Sunday 28 September 2025, which involved two cars and an e-bike.

The bike rider, 16-year-old Ryley Hutson, was pronounced dead at the scene on Chilwell Lane in Bramcote, Nottinghamshire. The road was closed as emergency services dealt with the incident and eyewitnesses reported an air ambulance landing in the close to the crash.

Now, in an update almost 10 months later, the Nottinghamshire Police has said Mr Cartwright, who is a serving police officer with Bedfordshire Police, has been charged with causing death by dangerous driving.

Mr Cartwright of Kettering, Northamptonshire is expected to appear before magistrates in Nottingham on 6 August 2026.

View 2 Images Flowers, candles, handwritten cards, and cans of the energy drink Monster were left at the side of the road (Image: Joseph Raynor/Reach PLC)

In an online fundraiser via GoFundMe created in the days following the incident, Ryley's aunt described the 16-year-old as being "full of life, laughter, and love".

"Our world has been shattered by the heart-breaking loss of 16-year-old Ryley, who tragically passed away in a fatal motorcycle accident," she said.

"Ryley was full of life, laughter, and love - a cheeky soul who left a lasting mark on everyone who had the privilege of knowing him."

At the time of the crash it was reported that a 30-year-old man had been arrested on suspicion of causing death by dangerous driving and released on police bail while investigations continued.

Detective Inspector Jamie Moore, of Nottinghamshire Police’s Serious Collision Investigation Unit, said: “This was a tragic incident which has had a devastating impact on Ryley's family.

"They have been updated about this important step in our investigation, and our thoughts remain with them."

Article continues below

An inquest was opened by coroner Amanda Bewley at Nottingham Coroner's Court on December 2 to look into the circumstances of Ryley's death.

Coroner Amanda Bewley told the short hearing that a post-mortem examination has established chest injuries as a provisional cause of death.

News.title: Animal rescue 'astonished' as missing cat Mr Star returns with gunshot wound
News.content:
Animal rescue 'astonished' as missing cat Mr Star returns with gunshot wound

Staff at Severn Valley Rescue, in Billingsley near Bridgnorth, Shropshire, have said they are in 'complete disbelief' after one of their cats, Mr Star, was shot with a rifle

View 2 Images Mr Star returned to Severn Valley Rescue limping in the early hours of Monday (Image: Severn Valley Rescue)

Staff at a Shropshire animal rescue have said they are in "complete disbelief" after one of their cats was shot with a rifle.

‌



Severn Valley Rescue, in Billingsley near Bridgnorth, said on Facebook that its ginger cat, Mr Star, went missing on Saturday morning and returned in the early hours of Monday limping badly and with a large, infected open wound. He was rushed to a vet, where he was sedated, given antibiotics and pain relief, and underwent X-rays.

‌



"To our complete disbelief, the remains of a bullet were found in Mr Star's shattered leg," the centre wrote in a Facebook post. "Not an air rifle. An actual rifle - the type you need a licence for. A real weapon."

‌



Mr Star's blood count was so low and he had lost so much blood that the vet was "astonished" he was still alive, the centre added.

View 2 Images Severn Valley Rescue has asked its neighbours to check their CCTV (Image: Facebook)

‌



Amanda Ball, one of the founders of Severn Valley Rescue, has set up a fundraiser on GoFundMe to help cover Mr Star's treatment, which is expected to run into the thousands.

The cat is currently receiving treatment to stabilise him ahead of a front leg amputation later this week. At the time of writing, the fundraiser has raised more than £500 - one-fifth of its £2,500 target.

"We are still checking all the CCTV and asking neighbours to do the same," Severn Valley Rescue said. "We have, of course, given all information to the police and preserved any evidence."

Article continues below

The centre urged anyone with information to come forward, particularly anyone who knows who may have been out shooting near Billingsley on July 17 or 18.

Severn Valley Rescue is a registered charity that looks after more than 200 animals. It was set up in 2008 under the name Shropshire Donkey Rescue. Its first official rescue was a donkey called One Eyed Jack, who, as his name suggests, has only one eye.

The rescue says it has since taken in many animals with disabilities, including a deaf pig, several three-legged cats, a one-eyed alpaca and a blind donkey.

News.title: BA pilots hit by food poisoning at 30,000ft with one 'incapacitated 'and put on oxygen
News.content:
BA pilots hit by food poisoning at 30,000ft with one 'incapacitated 'and put on oxygen

The flight deck crew who had breakfast while on a stopover in India, all fell ill with food poisoning with the worst hit having to be put on oxygen during the long-haul journey to Heathrow

View 2 Images Pilots on a BA flight fell ill after contracting food poisoning (Image: Getty Images)

British airways pilots were struck with food poisoning after a stopover - with one officer ‘incapacitated’.

‌



The pilots had broken their journey to the UK in India and had breakfast together in a nearby hotel lounge in Hyderabad, as well as drinking bottled water they bought from an outside vendor.

‌



One officer was hit hard and was left ‘incapacitated’ and had to be put on oxygen at 30,000 feet on the lengthy 10 and a half hour flight to London Heathrow. The other two pilots were able to continue working during the flight, but their symptoms progressed once the plane landed in Britain.

‌



British Airways confirmed passenger safety was not affected and that the flight operated safely. But insiders at pilots’ union Balpa reportedly said officials are angered as there was a large amount of previous complains surrounding the hygiene at their £130-a-night hotel.

View 2 Images BA confirmed they had launched an urgent investigation to ensure a similar ordeal does not happen again (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

‌



The pilots filed Air Safety reports and provided samples to ensure medical staff could pinpoint the direct source. British Airways is reportedly assessing the hotel options they have within the Southern Indian city of Hyderabad.

The airline said: “The welfare of our colleagues is a top priority and we are reviewing crew accommodation in this location following some isolated reports of sickness.

“During the flight one of our pilots became unwell. In line with established procedures, the aircraft continued safely to its destination and landed normally.

Article continues below

BA confirmed they had launched an investigation, adding: “The safety of our customers and crew is always our highest priority and at no point was the safety of the flight compromised.”

News.title: PC Harper's widow criticises early prisoner release plan as Burnham to review scheme
News.content:
The widow of PC Andrew Harper has described the possible early release of prisoners as "deplorable", following reports that two of his killers could be freed early.

Lissie Harper said politicians were "making decisions from behind a desk that will have real and lasting consequences" for the families of victims.

Prime Minister Andy Burnham earlier said he would review the Sentencing Act policy that from September would see thousands of offenders in England and Wales eligible to be released earlier.

Speaking on Wednesday, Burnham said: "I can't say that I can change the policy completely, but I will look at it in detail before we go further forward."

He acknowledged that there was "pressure on prisons places" and that a failure to invest in the prison system in the past had created "an unacceptable situation".

Jessie Cole and Albert Bowers were sentenced to 13 years in custody for manslaughter but could be released early under the new Sentencing Act.

PC Harper was killed after he was dragged to his death behind their getaway car. The car's driver, Henry Long, was jailed for 16 years for manslaughter but would not be eligible for early release.

Burnham's comments came after the mother of police officer Andrew Harper said the potential early release of two of her son's killers felt like an "insult".

In a separate statement released later on Wednesday, PC Harper's widow Lissie Harper said: "It has taken me years to rebuild a life that was torn apart in a matter of moments. Years to pick up the pieces left behind by three men whose actions robbed Andrew of his life and stole our future.

"It is deplorable to me that we have reached a point where releasing prisoners early is even considered acceptable. We speak of justice, accountability and standing with victims, yet decisions like this do the opposite."

The overcrowding of the prison estate has been a problem for several years and successive governments have released prisoners early in a bid to free up space.

Tens of thousands of inmates have been let out of prison to create more space in jails since 2024.

The Sentencing Act, which was passed by Sir Keir Starmer's government earlier this year, was designed to ease pressure on prisons, and will see some offenders spend less time in prison before release.

Burnham said: "I want to assure myself that everything has been looked at before this policy proceeds, and I can give that assurance that every single part of this I will look into with the justice secretary."

Concerning the case of PC Harper, he said: "I feel for the family it's an appalling crime that was committed."

He said the "main perpetrator" of his death would not be eligible for early release.

Burnham also said it was not acceptable to joke about early releases and that it was right Defence Secretary Wes Streeting had apologised for comments he made that were caught on camera.

News.title: Most bus fares in England to be capped at £2 from January
News.content:
The bus fare cap in England will revert to Â£2 from January, new prime minister Andy Burnham has announced.

The government says the policy, which is expected to cost more than Â£500m, will "help with the cost of living and give people the breathing space they need".

At the start of last year, the England-wide bus fare cap rose to Â£3 under Sir Keir Starmer's Labour government, although in Liverpool and Manchester fares were held at Â£2.

Burnham said affordable transport links were an essential, adding: "Lower fares will help people get to where they need to."

The measure gives people "a little bit of hope" in a time when many are grappling with higher living costs - especially after fuel costs spiked as a result of the US-Iran war, transport secretary Heidi Alexander told the BBC's Today programme.

However, she admitted the measure was "not the whole solution".

The new cap will take effect from January next year for fares on participating buses outside of London. The cost of a non-discounted single bus journey in London is Â£1.75.

The Burnham government said going back to a Â£2 cap should particularly help passengers in rural and coastal areas, where single fares can be higher.

The Campaign for Better Transport said rural areas were still suffering from fewer bus routes and services, adding that such areas had been more affected by council cut backs in the last decade than urban zones.

Services in those areas - as measured by vehicle miles - decreased by 18% between 2019 and 2024, according to the County Councils Network, which represents 39 unitary and county councils across England.

"What we need to see is the replacing of those lost services which have particularly affected those in rural areas," Campaign for Better Transport's Michael Solomon Williams said.

News.title: Ex-Southern Water boss among four charged over alleged plan to manipulate water quality tests
News.content:
The ex-chief executive of Southern Water has been charged with three others over an alleged plan to manipulate water quality tests to avoid paying financial penalties of about Â£45m, it can now be reported.

Matthew Wright is accused of conspiring to defraud the Environment Agency (EA) and water regulator Ofwat between 2012 and 2017, along with Philip Barker, Clive Massey and Mark Gregory, who also worked at the firm.

Wright's solicitor says he "denies all wrongdoing and has co-operated fully" with the EA's investigation.

Southern Water said the charges related to "a historic set of failures" uncovered in an internal investigation. It said it was a "completely different" company to a decade ago.

The EA asked a judge to issue a summons against the four, charging them with the offence, last year, but Wright launched a legal challenge, dismissed by two senior judges on Wednesday.

Massey, Gregory and Barker did not appear at the hearing in London and were not represented.

According to court documents, the allegations include arranging for wastewater to be removed from facilities by tankers in order to create "no flow" results.

This had been "with a view to covering up pollution and deceiving those whose function is to protect the public from such harm", prosecutors allege.

In his legal challenge, Wright's lawyers argued at the High Court in June that the EA did not have the power to issue the summons and it should be thrown out.

But the judges dismissed his claim and ruled restrictions previously preventing reporting of the legal challenge should be lifted.

Separate court listings showed the case against 60-year-old Wright, of Haslemere, Surrey; Barker, 57, of West Chiltington, West Sussex; Massey, 64, of Brandhill, Shropshire; and Gregory, 63, of Southampton, were scheduled to be heard at Medway Magistrates' Court on 14 July.

The four are accused of conspiring between 2012 and 2017 to defraud those conducting the environmental and financial regulation duties of Southern Water, including the EA and Ofwat, by "the implementation of artificial no-flow events at wastewater treatment works".

News.title: OpenAI says its AI went rogue and launched 'unprecedented' cyber-attack
News.content:
OpenAI has revealed some of its most advanced AI models went rogue and hacked a start-up after it lost control of them during a security test.

The ChatGPT-maker said its agent - an AI system which can operate alone after human instruction â was being tested in a controlled environment but, after finding weaknesses, was able to escape the test limits.

They targeted Hugging Face, one of the world's largest hubs for sharing AI models, gaining access to some internal company systems.

OpenAI said the incident was "unprecedented", external, and it was conducting an investigation alongside Hugging Face, whose boss Clement Delangue said in a post on X it was "mind-blowing that all of this happened autonomously".

"The investigation is ongoing, and we'll share more learnings from what might be the first incident of its kind," Delangue added.

A government spokesperson said the UK's AI Security Institute was studying the behaviour from the AI system seen in the incident and was continuing to work with OpenAI and other labs to improve safeguards.

They said organisations should step up their cyber-defences by taking steps such as enrolling in the government-backed Cyber Essentials certification scheme.

News.title: Prince George enjoys coastal fun in new video as he becomes a teenager
News.content:
A new video of Prince George has been released by Kensington Palace to mark his 13th birthday.

The video, external, showing a smiling prince waving at the camera in his sunglasses, playing cricket on the beach and climbing rocks, was accompanied by the caption: "Thank you for all the birthday wishes for George today!"

The video was shot in Cornwall at Easter, and follows a new photograph of George which was also published on social media on Wednesday.

George, the elder son of the Prince and Princess of Wales, is second in line to the throne.

News.title: Seized maternity notes not given to Lucy Letby defence for trial, BBC learns
News.content:
Maternity notes for the babies Lucy Letby has been convicted of murdering were not made available to her defence ahead of her trial, the BBC has learned.

The neonatal nurse was convicted of murdering and attempting to murder 14 babies at the Countess of Chester Hospital in 2015 and 2016.

File on 4 Investigates has discovered that maternity notes for the babies in the case - which include details of the mother's pregnancy, labour and birth - were seized by Cheshire Police. But they were not reviewed by the prosecution's chief medical expert or disclosed to Letby's defence.

The Crown Prosecution Service said Letby was convicted following two jury trials and that the Court of Appeal dismissed her argument that prosecution evidence was flawed.

Letby, originally of Hereford, is currently serving 15 whole life terms.

Since her trial, and subsequent retrial on one case, there have been concerns raised about some of the evidence presented to the jury.

One concern is that the maternity history of the babies in the case was not adequately considered.

Experts told the BBC that it is critical to fully assess the pregnancy, labour and delivery of a baby when determining why they collapsed and died.

Dr Dewi Evans, the chief medical witness for the prosecution, said the full maternity notes were not relevant to the case.

"I never saw any obstetric notes and I have no idea what happened to them," he said.

"I don't think that maternity care was a particular issue in the Letby case. I think most of the babies I dealt with were born in acceptable condition."

Evans said he did see brief maternity summaries - "usually a couple of paragraphs" - attached to each baby's neonatal notes.

News.title: Southampton boss Eckert charged by FA over Spygate
News.content:
Southampton head coach Tonda Eckert has been charged with misconduct by the Football Association for his role in the Spygate scandal.

Saints were kicked out of the Championship play-offs in May after admitting they spied on three clubs during the campaign.

An independent disciplinary commission ruled at the time that the espionage was authorised by Eckert and was a "contrived and determined plan from the top down".

Since then the club has been the subject of an investigation by the FA, looking into who participated in the spying and assessing the culpability of those who knew it was happening.

The FA said, external Eckert "has been charged with three breaches of FA rule E3.1 in relation to misconduct between December 2025 and May 2026".

Southampton beat Middlesbrough over two legs in the play-off semi-final but, after Saints' expulsion, Boro were reinstated to the final and went on to lose to Hull City.

The English Football League (EFL) expelled Southampton from the play-offs after they admitted watching training sessions involving Oxford United and Ipswich Town, in addition to filming Middlesbrough before the semi-final.

The EFL can only take action against its member clubs but the FA can punish individuals and hand out bans.

The FA said it is "alleged that the head coach acted in an improper manner and/or brought the game into disrepute by directing and/or authorising the observation of training sessions" of these games.

Eckert has until next Tuesday to respond.

In a statement, Southampton said, external they and Eckert "acknowledge today's charges from the FA relating to a breach of rule E3.1".

The club added: "Tonda and the club will continue to co-operate fully and openly with the FA.

"Our focus remains on preparations for the 2026-27 Championship season. The club remains fully supportive of Tonda and his staff as we work towards our ambition of returning to the Premier League.

"We are unable to comment further while the process remains ongoing, but we will provide an update to supporters as soon as we are in a position to do so."

News.title: Modelling scout linked to Epstein found dead in Paris
News.content:
A modelling scout linked to the late convicted sex offender Jeffrey Epstein has been found dead at his home.

Daniel Siad, 69, was discovered on Monday in Colombes, a north-west suburb of Paris, the Nanterre prosecutor's office confirmed to the BBC.

An investigation to determine the cause of death was opened on Monday evening, the office said, adding that a post-mortem examination would be carried out.

Siad's name appeared thousands of times in the Epstein files released by the US government. He denied knowing of the threat Epstein had posed.

His lawyer stressed that Siad, who had been the subject of several complaints in France including allegations of rape, had "never been prosecuted".

"He is dead and he was innocent," MÃ©nya Arab-Tigrine said in a statement.

Epstein victim Anya - not her real name - previously told the BBC that Siad had introduced her to Epstein.

"It was a complete set-up," she said, describing Siad as "essentially a professional trafficker".

During one email to Epstein released in the files, Siad wrote in badly spelled English: "In This busyness I feel like fisherman some time I cache quick, some time no fish."

Ahead of a BBC investigation on the subject published on Saturday, Arab-Tigrine had said her client was not available for comment.

However, in a recent CNN interview, Siad said he had not known the women were being abused by Epstein. "I trusted him, I believed this guy is a professional person," he said.

The first complaints against Siad in France were filed in February. He denied wrongdoing in multiple recent media interviews, telling BFMTV in May: "I have never raped anyone in my life."

Lawyers for the former model who made the first complaint said they were "stunned" by his death.

"We are at a loss for words to describe the anger and sadness we feel," they said, with alleged victims "denied a criminal trial".

The lawyers said they felt "immense anger toward the Paris Public Prosecutor's Office, which announced last February that it was opening an investigation into Jeffrey Epstein's French accomplices".

They accused the office of "scandalous" inaction which they said demonstrated "the public authorities' contempt for victims of sexual crimes, even when these crimes are linked to the human trafficking network established by Epstein and his accomplices".

The BBC has contacted the prosecutor's office for comment.

Another former model who gave a deposition to police in June as part of the investigation into Siad told the BBC his death meant any information he might have had about Epstein was now lost.

"An important link in the chain has just vanished into thin air, without there even having been a chance to recover the information Daniel Siad might have possessed, given that he was never questioned," she said.

"Too much time has been lost... and it is yet another way for the leads to go cold. I hope we won't have to wait another seven years to see his home searched, even though I think it is already too late."

Anne-Claire Le Jeune, who represents six women who made complaints about Siad, said victims had been deprived of justice: "My clients found the strength to break a particularly heavy silence, given Daniel Siad's ties to Jeffrey Epstein

"They faced every stage of the proceedings with remarkable courage.

"It is deeply regrettable that the slow pace of the investigation resulted in his death before he could be questioned or taken into police custody, thereby depriving the victims of a crucial step in their pursuit of truth and justice."

Another associate of Epstein, French modelling agent Jean-Luc Brunel, was found hanged in his Paris prison cell in 2022.

The 76-year-old had been held in custody for more than a year as he was investigated on suspicion of the rape of minors and trafficking of minors for sexual exploitation. Brunel denied any wrongdoing.

Brunel founded MC2 Model Management with funding from Epstein and was suspected of transporting and housing girls or young women for Epstein.

Epstein, 66, died by suicide in a New York jail cell in 2019 as he awaited a federal trial for sex trafficking.

News.title: Some food prices have fallen – but inflation expected to rise from here
News.content:
Food prices are rising at their slowest rate in nearly two years, as the cost of some staples such as margarine and sugar have gone down.

Supermarket price wars have helped drive down prices in the year to June, the industry says, as retailers work to tempt customers with summer deals.

Inflation in the UK overall has fallen to 2.6% in the year to June, down from 2.8% in the year to May, according to the Office for National Statistics (ONS), driven largely by lower fuel and food prices.
