Sports.title: England cannot afford trip to amputee World Cup – and the FA will not help
Sports.content:
Every time Scott Rogers walks into St George’s Park there is a sign on the wall that catches his eye. It boasts that the 330-acre site is the proud home of all England’s football teams. “I look at it every time and go, ‘Well, not all of them’,” Rogers says.

As head coach, Rogers guided the England men’s amputee team to the Nations League trophy in 2023. But while the Football Association funds six para national teams, amputee football is not among them.

Now one of the world’s leading amputee nations is struggling to raise enough money to compete at the men’s World Cup in Mexico in November. England earned £21.5m in prize money for finishing third in the World Cup and got £1.1m in preparation funds. The amputee side are trying to scrape together £50,000 to cover their tournament costs.

“The FA say they’re funded for a certain amount of para teams and at the moment there isn’t the funding to bring amputee football into the fold,” Rogers says. “We’re Nations League champions, and there’s a chance we won’t go to this World Cup. For an England team at the top of the game to miss a World Cup due to funding, it doesn’t sit right.”

The amputee programme was under the FA umbrella until 2006, when the governing body cut funding. “That left a lot of bad feeling at the time,” Rogers says.

They set up as a charity and have built a thriving structure. The women’s team reached the quarter-finals of the inaugural World Cup in 2024. The junior system has more than 70 players aged four to 17. They have doctors, strength and conditioning coaches, analysts, technical coaches. It is run by volunteers and funded by donations.

Rogers, a former youth coach at Wigan and Blackburn, became involved in 2000. “Whatever I’d do with an under-18 elite able-bodied team, I’d do with these lads because they were incredible,” he says.

View image in fullscreen Scott Rogers (fourth from left) coached England’s men’s amputee team for a year and helped them win the Nations League. Photograph: LAJ Photography

“When people think about amputee football, they probably imagine it’s slow and laborious. It’s the opposite: fast-paced, brutal at times. They snap crutches almost every game. I fell in love with it.”

FA representatives shadowed the team at the 2022 World Cup and were impressed. But though they made a funding offer, it fell short of what was in place. “All the signs were good,” Rogers says. But the offer would have reduced training frequency and cut the number of coaches and specialists. It was declined. Coming back under the FA umbrella while continuing to take money from other sources was not an option, Rogers says.

When Owen Coyle Jr – son of the former Burnley manager – stepped down as head coach in 2023, Rogers took over. Previously, players each had to raise £1,500 to secure their place for tournaments, but Rogers scrapped the requirement.

An appearance on ITV’s Good Morning Britain provided the funding boost to play at Euro 2024, their pot rising from £4,000 of their £40,000 target to more than £50,000 within hours. For the World Cup this year, they are not even halfway to the £50,000 needed.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

“These people don’t get paid for playing, they have jobs,” Rogers says. “If the programme isn’t of a certain level, what’s the incentive to continue to play? They sacrifice holidays with their families.”

View image in fullscreen Rhyce Ramsden (right) flies into an attempted tackle on fellow England amputee player Nathan Fisher (left) during a training session. Photograph: LAJ Photography

Rogers, who stepped down as head coach in 2024 but remains heavily involved, says even £50,000 a year from the FA would go a long way. “When you look at the funding within the FA and the money involved in football, what we’re asking for to make an amazing programme is a drop in the ocean.”

The amputee players are paying for their own flights for a game in Ireland next month. “It’s there, it’s ready to go,” Rogers says. “But the danger is if we don’t secure long-term funding soon – because we can’t keep going on telly, it’s a model that won’t continue to work – I feel that we’re going to start to fall away.”

Rogers says there are “brilliant” people at the FA who run the para programme and want amputee football included, but cannot secure the funding from above. “There are always ongoing conversations with the FA and it’s not a bad relationship. But unless something changes and somebody stands up and goes: ‘Listen, this can’t happen any more,’ I think it’ll be ground into the into the ground when we’re on the verge of something incredibly special.”

An FA spokesperson said: “We continue to work closely with the England Amputee Football Association to support, identify and help deliver their key priorities over the coming season, and the continued development of amputee football in England.”

Sports.title: Man City confident of reaching deal for World Cup sensation Ayyoub Bouaddi
Sports.content:
Manchester City are increasingly hopeful of signing Lille midfielder Ayyoub Bouaddi, talkSPORT understands.

Bouaddi, who was a breakout star for Morocco at the World Cup, has been a target for multiple Premier League giants this summer.



4 City are confident they can complete the signing of Bouaddi this summer Credit: Getty

The teenage sensation had previously held talks with Arsenal and Liverpool, while Chelsea were among those tracking him.

However, it's Man City who believe they are close to a deal, with Lille understood to be wanting £85.3million for their star.

And it is believed that City not to be loaning Bouaddi back to the Ligue 1 side to continue his development.



This comes after Lille made it clear that they preferred to delay a transfer of the 18-year-old by a year.

Good to Bouadd

The French side are prepared to sell him, but have been offering a discounted deal if clubs were open to a loan back or pre-agreement.



If City were to let Bouaddi stay with his current team for another year, they could get a deal done for £68.2m instead.

But that doesn't seem like the case, with Enzo Maresca and co. wanting the midfielder to join straight away and be part of the squad.



talkSPORT's Ben Jacobs revealed on July 1: "This is a fascinating transfer story because Lille are prepared to sell, but they heavily favour a deal for 2027, clubs, and Manchester City, have shown they are willing to at least discuss this."

"It's €80m [£68.2m] at the moment, but could come down for those that say to Lille a loan back or pre-agreement," he added.

"It's €100m [£85.3m] for other clubs that want an immediate transfer, so that's going to be one to watch."

4 Bouaddi starred for Morocco at the World Cup and dominated against Brazil in the 1-1 draw Credit: Getty



4 The teenagers started in five matches in North America

Bouaddi's brilliant summer

Man City are set to move for Bouaddi following his incredible World Cup campaign, which saw him catch the eye.

He started every game but one for Morocco at the tournament in North America.

His performance against Brazil instantly had fans in awe, as he stood out against the South American giants.



Bouaddi had the most touches (88), won the most duels (11) and completed the most successful passes in the opposition’s half (30).

His 60 completed passes also made him the second youngest player to complete over 50 passes in a World Cup match in 60 years.

And he would go on to impress again against Scotland, the Netherlands and Canada before struggling against France.

4 Bouaddi could end up being Man City's next midfield arrival after Anderson Credit: Shutterstock Editorial



But Bouaddi remains one of the most sought-after midfielders on the planet, with City hoping to get a deal over the line.

Maresca, who is set for his first campaign in charge, is looking to bolster his midfield after losing Bernardo Silva.

He has already secured the £116m signing of Elliot Anderson, but Bouaddi may also join the talented ranks.

City have signed Anderson, Jeremy Monga, Pierce Charles and Mathys Detourbet so far this summer.

Sports.title: Axel Disasi offered Chelsea escape route as two European clubs express interest
Sports.content:
Chelsea centre-back Axel Disasi is attracting interest from AC Milan and Roma, talkSPORT understands.

The 28-year-old is not in the Blues' plans going forward following the arrival of new boss Xabi Alonso.



2 Disasi's three-year stay at Chelsea could be coming to an end this summer Credit: Getty

Disasi has not reported back for Chelsea pre-season training as both he and the club look for him to find a new team.

Valued at around £25million by the west London outfit, Chelsea stand to make a loss on him.

Signed from Monaco in 2023 for £38m, the defender has failed to hold down a regular starting spot at Stamford Bridge.



Having featured in 44 games in his opening season - scoring on his debut in a 1-1 draw with Liverpool - he quickly soon fell out of favour.

The five-cap France international was shipped off on loan to Aston Villa for the second half of the 2024/25 term - appearing in seven Premier League games.



And having failed to feature for Chelsea in the first half of last season, he then joined West Ham on loan.

Disasi quickly endeared himself to the Hammers faithful as he slotted in alongside Konstantinos Mavropanos in the heart of the back four.



While he scored once from 17 games across all competitions, he ultimately failed to help West Ham remain in the top-flight.

Axel to grind

talkSPORT understands that the east London side had wanted to bring Disasi back to the London Stadium.

However, the player has no desire in competing in the Championship - opening the door to a potential move to Italy.

2 Disasi impressed for West Ham from his 14 Premier League outings



Both Roma and Milan are willing to offer Disasi an escape route from his Chelsea nightmare.

Roma can offer the ex-Reims star Champions League football, where he would reunite with former Villa teammate Donyell Malen.

Meanwhile, Milan will be plying their trade in the Europa League.

The Rossoneri have made it a habit in recent years to raid Chelsea for players in either permanent transfers or loan deals.

Christian Pulisic, Fikayo Tomori, Ruben Loftus-Cheek, Olivier Giroud, Tiemoue Bakayoko, Joao Felix and Christopher Nkunku have all made the direct switch since 2021.



Should Disasi be sold, Chelsea could look to replace him with another French centre-back in Crystal Palace's Maxence Lacroix.

Sports.title: Why Alejandro Garnacho could trump Marcus Rashford as Unai Emery’s best Aston Villa resurrection act yet
Sports.content:
Why Alejandro Garnacho could trump Marcus Rashford as Unai Emery’s best Aston Villa resurrection act yet

It's become a common theme of Unai Emery's tenure at Aston Villa.

In the last two seasons, the Spaniard has become enamoured with a player who, for whatever reason, has lost their way.

6 Emery has worked with a number of high-profile stars over the years Credit: Getty

Let's rewind to the summer of 2024, when Villa were preparing for their maiden Champions League campaign following the competition's re-brand in 1991.

One Fel swoop

Joao Felix, who had joined Atletico Madrid from Benfica in an eye-watering £113million deal five years earlier, was high in Emery's thinking.

But Villa were not targeting the same Felix that convinced Atleti to fork out a nine-figure sum.

As talented as Felix may have been, there were questions over his consistency and effort.

"He (Felix) has all the qualities to be an incredible player, but as good as you are, if you don't work, it's not enough," Saul Niguez, Felix's former teammate at Atleti, previously said on Spanish radio.

Despite Emery's keenness to sign Felix across multiple transfer windows, underpinned by the Spaniard's belief he could revive the stuttering career of the 2019 Golden Boy, a deal never came to fruition.

Felix, 26, now plies his trade with Al-Nassr in Saudi Arabia.

Emery's not-so-Rash decision

We now move to January 2025, where Villa had progressed to the knockout stage of the Champions League and were looking to finish the Premier League campaign strongly.

Marcus Rashford had been frozen out at Manchester United by then-manager Ruben Amorim.

Their relationship was so strained, Amorim said he would rather have his then-63-year-old goalkeeping coach Jorge Vital be among the substitutes over Rashford, who 'doesn't give the maximum every day'.

6 Rashford registered 10 goal contributions in 17 games for Villa Credit: Getty

But Emery spotted an opportunity to get a forward blessed with remarkable pace and quality back to his best.

"My challenge with him is huge," Emery said after Rashford moved to Villa on loan until the end of the season.

Marco Asensio, who Emery unsuccessfully pushed to sign in the summer of 2023, also arrived on loan.

Asensio, a three-time Champions League winner with Real Madrid, chose Paris Saint-Germain over Villa in 2023 but had struggled for game time with the French side.

Working under Emery ultimately proved to be a wise move for Rashford.

He quickly regained his spot in the England squad and spent last season on loan with Barcelona, although he is somewhat back to square one after they opted not to make the move permanent.

6 Rashford assisted four of Asensio's goals for Villa, proving Emery's restorative powers Credit: Getty

Villa did attempt to re-sign Asensio after his loan spell ended but could not complete a deal, as the attacking midfielder eventually moved to Turkish giants Fenerbahce.

The Don

The summer of 2025 brought yet another high-profile name, at least on paper, to Villa Park.

Jadon Sancho joined Manchester United from Borussia Dortmund in July 2021 for an estimated £73m.

It was a monumental fee for Sancho, who was just 21 years old at the time.

But - there's a theme here, isn't there - the big-money switch did not go to plan for either party.

After two seasons where he struggled to live up to the lofty price tag, Sancho's woes with United came to a head in September 2024 when the forward was forced to train away from the first team until a 'squad discipline issue' was resolved.

6 In the last three seasons, Sancho has scored just nine goals Credit: Getty

Mixed loan spells with Dortmund and Chelsea followed before he wound up at Villa on deadline day.

However, the 26-year-old struggled to make his mark under Emery, registering one goal and three assists from 39 appearances across all competitions.

Sancho was later released by United and remains a free agent.

Garna do it once more?

Which brings us to this transfer window, where Emery is, yet again, about to embark on yet another resurrection act.

This time, it's Chelsea winger Alejandro Garnacho, who is poised to join Villa on loan but with a conditional obligation to buy clause.

Emery previously tried to land the Argentinian last summer when it was clear he had no future at Old Trafford, only for Garnacho to join Chelsea instead.

6 With Morgan Rogers joining Chelsea, Garnacho has been pushed further out the exit door Credit: Getty

But the Blues are already looking to offload Garnacho after just one season in which he scored eight goals and assisted four.

Given the timing of Garnacho's potential move compared to the deadline day rush of Sancho, Emery's fingerprints are all over this deal and there's a high chance the winger would slot straight in to Villa's starting line-up.

Yet it's one that former Premier League stalwart Kevin Nolan couldn't quite wrap his head around, even if Emery backs himself to revive the 22-year-old.

Nolan, who admitted he doesn't know Garnacho personally, said: "He looks like a problem child, he looks like a problem if he's not playing, he'll throw his toys out of the pram if it's not going too well for him.

"I think if you've got him on board and you've got your arm around him and everything else and if everything suits him, I think he's a real big and good player.

"But is he big enough for Unai Emery to sort of go, 'I'll take him because I'll be able to get the best out of him?'"

6 Emery has backed himself to get the best out of Garnacho, who scored once in the league last term Credit: Getty

At age 22, time is certainly on Garnacho's side to prove his doubters wrong and enjoy a prosperous career.

But that relies heavily on Emery successfully performing yet another revival act.

If the Villa boss can do just that, it might be one of his best managerial feats yet.

Sports.title: Top ten most expensive summer transfers so far: Chelsea, Man City and Spurs all confirm £100m deals
Sports.content:
Top ten most expensive summer transfers so far: Chelsea, Man City and Spurs all confirm £100m deals

Premier League clubs have been hard at work splashing the cash this summer, with three clubs already completing nine-figure deals.

The transfer record for a British player has been broken with Chelsea sealing the £117million capture of Morgan Rogers from Aston Villa.

11 Rogers has joined Chelsea in a blockbuster deal

The 2026 summer window officially opened on June 15, with talkSPORT.com already providing a completed list of every deal.

Due to certain PSR constraints, some initial-loan agreements in previous windows have since become permanent this summer.

The rising inflation in the transfer market also means relegation is no longer a signal for clubs to poach key players on the cheap.

With that in mind, teams have had to open up their chequebooks. Below are the top 10 most expensive arrivals in the Premier League...

10. Luka Vuskovic (Tottenham to Brighton) – £46m

The Seagulls have built a reputation for signing young gems for moderate prices before later selling them on for big profits.

However, Fabian Hurzeler's men were forced to break their club record to prize Croatia defender Vuskovic from Tottenham.

The total deal for the 19-year-old includes bonuses that take the price above £50m, with the centre-back signing a five-year contract.

Spurs had previously knocked back two offers worth £30m and £35m for Vuskovic, who never played a competitive game in north London.

However, Vuskovic, labelled as a generational talent, underlined his standing as one of Europe's brightest young players while out on loan at Hamburg last season.

11 Vuskovic came head-to-head with England in Croatia's opening World Cup game Credit: Getty

9. Marco Palestra (Atalanta to Chelsea) - £47m

The Blues moved fast to hijack Inter Milan's move for the 21-year-old right-back, who has signed a six-year deal at Stamford Bridge.

The Atalanta academy graduate spent last season on loan at Cagliari and was named Serie A's defender of the year.

He scored once and registered four assists across 37 appearances in Italy's top-flight and is an ideal fit for Xabi Alonso's wing-back system.

Palestra made his senior international debut in March and earned his second cap in Italy's World Cup play-off final defeat to Bosnia.

The defender is already in Chelsea's first-team training and is expected to be part of their pre-season tour in Australia and Asia.

11 Palestra became the first signing of the Xabi Alonso era at Stamford Bridge Credit: Getty

8) Andrey Santos (Chelsea to Manchester United) – £50m

talkSPORT understands the Red Devils have paid £48m plus £2m in achievable add-ons to land the Brazilian midfielder from the Blues.

Newcastle were also understood to be keen on Chelsea's former No.17, who has now taken the same shirt number at Old Trafford.

The 22-year-old only made 13 Premier League starts last season, nearly half of which came under his ex-Strasbourg manager Liam Rosenior, during the latter's four-month tenure as Chelsea boss.

United prioritised central midfield reinforcements this summer following Casemiro's exit, with Manuel Ugarte also rupturing his anterior cruciate ligament at the World Cup.

11 Man United's new signing Andrey Santos made his unofficial debut against Wrexham in Helsinki Credit: Getty

7) Jan Paul van Hecke (Brighton to Tottenham) – £52m

The Netherlands defender's move to Spurs wasn't part of the deal that saw Vuskovic head in the opposite direction.

However, on the balance sheet, Roberto De Zerbi reunited with his former Brighton player for a nominal fee, all things considered.

Tottenham were persistent in their bid to land Van Hecke, with Seagulls CEO Paul Barber revealing on talkSPORT that the Lilywhites had two previous bids rejected.

The Dutchman, who cost Brighton just £1.8m from NAC Breda in 2020, was entering the final year of his contract with Hurzeler's side.

11 De Zerbi has worked with the Dutch defender before on the south coast Credit: AFP

6) Johan Manzambi (Freiburg to Aston Villa) - £52m

Unai Emery's side have been involved in the biggest transfer of the summer so far, but have also broken their club record on a player.

The West Midlands club snapped up Manzambi for £52m, which surpassed the £50m forked out to land Amadou Onana in 2024.

Newcastle were close to signing the midfielder, having agreed a deal in principle with Freiburg for £51m, before Villa swooped in.

The 20-year-old played against Villa in the Europa League final, while he also scored three goals for Switzerland in the World Cup.

11 Villa broke their transfer record to sign the Switzerland midfielder Credit: Getty Images

5) Jeremy Jacquet (Rennes to Liverpool) – £60m

Liverpool completed the biggest deal of the winter window's deadline day by beating Chelsea to land the France U21 international.

talkSPORT understands that the Reds agreed an initial £55m to sign Jacquet, with a further £5m to be paid in potential add-ons.

A move for the defender eclipsed the £52m fee spent by Manchester City on Jeremy Doku in 2023 to become Rennes' record sale.

However, the 21-year-old spent the second half of last season at his boyhood club, with a move to Anfield only becoming official on July 1.

11 Jacquet inherited Ibrahima Konate's No.5 shirt at Liverpool Credit: Getty

4) Mateus Fernandes (West Ham to Tottenham) – £85m

Spurs have broken their transfer record twice this summer, the first of which saw Fernandes arrive from their relegated London rivals.

The 22-year-old was one of the standout Premier League midfielders last season, despite West Ham's struggles.

He scored five top-flight goals and registered four assists in 41 appearances but missed out on Portugal's World Cup squad.

However, Troy Deeney told talkSPORT that he questioned whether Fernandes was really the player to 'change the mentality' at Tottenham after his successive relegations, having also failed to beat the drop at Southampton.

11 Spurs beat off competition from Manchester United to secure Fernandes' signature Credit: Shutterstock Editorial

3) Sandro Tonali (Newcastle to Tottenham) – £100m

Spurs shattered their transfer record again to poach the Italian from Newcastle less than a week after unveiling Fernandes.

Tonali joined De Zerbi's side in a £100m deal - an initial £92.5m fee with £7.5m in proposed add-ons.

The 26-year-old made 110 appearances across his three seasons with Newcastle after his reported £52m move from AC Milan in July 2023.

But he was accused by talkSPORT Breakfast co-host Gabriel Agbonlahor of joining Tottenham 'for the big bucks'.

11 Tonali is the latest key player to leave St. James' Park after signing for Tottenham Credit: Shutterstock Editorial

2) Elliot Anderson (Nottingham Forest to Manchester City) – £116m

Man City were the first of two clubs to break the transfer record for a British player following their capture of Anderson at the start of July.

The England international sealed his move to the Etihad Stadium from Nottingham Forest for a fixed £116m fee while at the World Cup.

Forest have tried to claim the deal is worth a total of £130m, which would eclipse the Premier League transfer record set by Liverpool's £125m signing of Alexander Isak, but City dispute this.

Anderson featured in all of England's games during their run to third at the World Cup - their best finish at the tournament since 1966.

11 Anderson put in some heroic midfield performances Credit: talKSPORT

1) Morgan Rogers (Aston Villa to Chelsea) - £117m

Anderson's reign as the most expensive British player lasted mere weeks as his England teammate Rogers took the crown.

The 23-year-old was the leading target at Arsenal, but he has now signed a six-year deal, with the option of another 12 months, at their London rivals Chelsea.

"I'm so excited," Rogers said on the move.

"For me, Chelsea are the biggest club in London and a club I've always admired since I was a kid.

11 Rogers made three starts and a further four sub appearances for England at the World Cup Credit: Getty

"I'm really excited about the project with the new manager, the players we've got and where the club is heading. That's why I'm here, and I can't wait to get started.

"The way the club wants to go and how it wants to move forward, it's something I want to be a part of, and I think it was just perfect for me.

"I'm a free spirit, free-flowing footballer. I like to take risks, make things happen, change games. Whatever that may take. Just can't wait to get started."

Sports.title: When is Champions League draw? Manchester United face club first in new European campaign
Sports.content:
When is Champions League draw? Manchester United face club first in new European campaign

The new Champions League campaign is already getting close as Europe's elite await the league phase draw.

Paris Saint-Germain beat Arsenal on penalties at the end of May to become back-to-back winners of the elite competition.



3 PSG won the Champions League last season with a penalty victory over Arsenal Credit: Getty

The 2025/26 final doesn't feel very long ago at all, but eyes are already moving on to the new season of action across Europe.

In fact, the new Champions League campaign has actually already started, with the qualifying rounds getting going in early July.

They will continue into August to decide the clubs that make it through to the full competition before the main draw.



Premier League champions Arsenal are going to be aiming to go one better this year, while Manchester City, Liverpool and Aston Villa will all be back in action in UEFA's elite competition again too.

Manchester United have also returned to the Champions League for the first time since the 2023/24 campaign.



It will be Man United's debut in the competition's new format, as they will be part of the league phase for the first time since its introduction by UEFA two seasons ago.

When is the Champions League draw?

The Champions League league phase draw will be held on Thursday, August 27 at UEFA's headquarters in Nyon, Switzerland.



A start time for the draw is yet to be confirmed but will likely be 11am UK time.

The draw will include the 36 qualified clubs, with each team finding out their eight opponents for the league phase.

Each side will play four home games and four away games.

3 The 2026/27 league phase draw takes place at the end of August Credit: Getty

How to follow Champions League draw

talkSPORT and talkSPORT.com will be across all the latest news from the draw.



Listen talkSPORT through the website or find us on DAB digital radio through your smart speaker and on 1089 or 1053 AM.

Download and listen to all our live commentaries via the talkSPORT app.

For the latest odds and bet boosts for every big event, visit talkSPORT BET.

Subscribe to the talkSPORT YouTube channel for news, views and analysis plus our regular goals show and for more, 



The Champions League league phase draw is likely to be shown live on TNT Sports and HBO Max, as well as on UEFA TV.

Sports.title: John Stones linked with Chelsea and Arsenal but told he’d be perfect signing for Premier League rival instead
Sports.content:
John Stones linked with Chelsea and Arsenal but told he’d be perfect signing for Premier League rival instead

Liverpool have been urged to sign John Stones on a free transfer this summer.

The England defender is a free agent after leaving Manchester City when his contract expired at the end of June.

3 Free agent Stones is already attracting interest from Chelsea and Arsenal Credit: Getty

Stones departed the Etihad Stadium following ten years with the club having signed from Everton in 2016.

During that time, he won 19 trophies including six Premier League titles, the Champions League and the Club World Cup.

The 32-year-old is already attracting interest after making five appearances for the Three Lions on their run to the World Cup semi-finals.

talkSPORT understands that Chelsea are currently weighing up a move for Stones.

Meanwhile, Arsenal have also shown interest in a potential move for the centre-back.

However, Liverpool have now been told the former Everton man would be a perfect fit for Andoni Iraola's side.

Liverpool to sign Stones?

Reds fan and Peterborough United chairman Darragh MacAnthony made the claim live on talkSPORT on Wednesday.

Speaking to Alex Crook, he explained: "I’d love Liverpool to sign him.

"We have two centre-backs, young ones, paid a lot of money for one (Jeremy Jacquet) and a lot of money for the other one (Giovanni Leoni), who did his ACL last year.

"We obviously we have (Virgil) Van Dijk and obviously then Joe Gomez has got injury-proneness to his resume.

3 MacAnthony has urged Liverpool to offer Stones a two-year deal this summer Credit: talkSPORT

"I would love Stones with Van Dijk, just to bed in those two younger players who were coming back from injury.

"What are you going to pay him? I don’t know, £2million? £3million, £4million, £5million-a-year?"

Defensive headache

Ibrahima Konate's departure to Real Madrid on a free transfer has left Liverpool with just four senior centre-backs ahead of next season.

Amongst them are youngsters Jacquet and Leoni, who both faced significant injury lay-offs last season.

New signing Jacquet missed the final three months of his campaign with Rennes due to a shoulder injury.

Meanwhile, Leoni has been sidelined since suffering a torn ACL on his Liverpool debut in September.

3 Stones won six Premier League titles during ten years at City as he left at the end of June Credit: Getty

Although both players are expected to be fit in time for the start of the new season, MacAnthony is keen for Stones to add to the experience of Van Dijk and Gomez.

Asked if he could be offered a 'pay-as-you-play' deal, he added: "No, he’s not going to take that.

"You can give him a two-year deal and probably pay him £10-12million in total. That’s a bargain.

"After the first game, I thought he got better as the World Cup went on."

Stones started England's opening win over Croatia before substitute appearances against DR Congo and Mexico in the knockout stage.

He later returned to the starting XI for the quarter-final win over Norway and kept his place against Argentina in the last four.

Sports.title: Ally McCoist asked if he would replace Steve Clarke as Scotland manager
Sports.content:
Ally McCoist asked if he would replace Steve Clarke as Scotland manager

Ally McCoist admitted he would never turn down the chance to manage Scotland, as the hunt for Steve Clarke's successor continues.

Clarke immediately stepped down as Tartan Army boss after the national team's disappointing World Cup group stage exit, with no replacement being announced as yet.



5 Steve Clarke called time on his seven-year stint as Scotland boss after their World Cup exit Credit: Getty

After guiding Scotland to their first World Cup appearance in 28 years, the 62-year-old endured a difficult summer in North America.

His side finished the group stage as the 11th best third-place team and missed out on a place in the last 32 on goal difference.

With Clarke stepping down just moments after the nation's tournament fate was sealed, a number of names have been floated as potential candidates for the role.



So far, ex-Celtic boss Ange Postecoglou has been tipped for the role, as well as Everton's David Moyes, and recently departed Portugal manager Roberto Martinez.

Meanwhile, Clarke's assistant at Scotland, Steven Naismith, has also been backed to be promoted to the manager's role.



Can't say no

As speculation continues over who will be next to lead Scotland, the question was put to talkSPORT's very own McCoist over whether he would fancy his chances of taking the team forward.

The Rangers icon is no stranger to the Tartan Army dugout, having previously been assistant to the late Walter Smith between 2004 and 2007.



On Wednesday's talkSPORT Breakfast, presenter Shebahn Aherne quizzed: "In all honesty, Ally do you think you could do it?"

To this, McCoist quipped: “I'd need to give up talkSPORT for at least a couple of days a week would I not?"

Work commitments aside, the much-loved Scot insisted he would jump at a return to the national team set-up, despite not having managed since his departure as Rangers boss in 2015.

5 Steven Naismith was named Steve Clarke's Scotland assistant in August 2025 Credit: getty



5 McCoist worked alongside Scottish footballing icons in Walter Smith and Tommy Burns during his last stint in the national team set-up Credit: Getty

Answering honestly, he said: "I mean, they've got a bit of time to pick and digest and get whoever they want, but I don't know whether that ship's sailed, Shebahn, to be honest with you.

“I don't know, but you never knock back your country, do you? That's for sure, no matter what it is.”

On his previous spell with Scotland, McCoist said: “I loved it when Walter was in and he took Tommy [Burns] and myself as his assistants in the national team, it was one of the best periods, selfishly in my own life. I loved it.



“And Tam was obviously an absolute diamond, brilliant to work with and Walter - you know what I think of Walter - we had a great wee period there and the team did really, really well."

McCoist: Future is bright

McCoist was also enthusiastic about the prospect of the potential for a home European Championship, with England, Scotland, Wales and Ireland hosting the 2028 edition.

Due to tournament regulations, only two host nations are able to receive automatic qualification.

5 McCoist's last managerial gig came at Rangers between 2011 and 2014 Credit: Getty



But after Scotland qualified for each of the last two European campaigns, McCoist had plenty of optimism for the national team.

He said: “The great thing that we've got now, that we didn't have maybe about 10, 15 years ago, I wouldn't say the entire nation wasn't in love with the football team, but it had lost a little bit of love.

"That's back, it's clearly back and it's back in abundance. So we'll want to carry on.

“The next Euros are obviously in the home nations, so you clearly want to be part of that.



"I think there's two that qualify out of four and all that, and then if there's any other qualifications, a bit complicated, but you'd like to think we can qualify."

Ally's Scotland boss tip

After insisting he would always be open to the Scotland job, McCoist then claimed Falkirk boss John McGlynn could be in line for the role.

5 John McGlynn has guided Falkirk from Scottish League One to the Premiership in the last two years Credit: Getty

Three-time PFA Scotland Manager of the Year has been heavily linked with the role after guiding Falkirk to an impressive sixth-place Scottish Premiership finish last season.



McCoist explained: “I'm hearing John McGlynn at Falkirk has got a chance. I for one wouldn't think that was a bad idea, they did a brilliant job.

"They were brilliant last year, Falkirk and Motherwell in particular, were two great success stories last year. I've known John for a long, long time, he's just a good, hard-working, honest footballing man.

“We could do a lot worse than John, but I don't think there's any outstanding candidates at the moment.

“I think Derek McInnes would have been the obvious one, obviously before he got the Rangers job.”

Sports.title: Jurgen Klopp set to appoint his former player as Germany assistant coach
Sports.content:
Jurgen Klopp set to appoint his former player as Germany assistant coach

Sven Bender is reportedly set to become Jurgen Klopp's assistant manager with the Germany national team.

The former Liverpool boss will be unveiled as Julian Nagelsmann's successor this week.



4 Klopp's Germany backroom team is taking shape ahead of his appointment as manager Credit: Getty

Klopp is understood to have agreed terms on a four-year deal through to the end of the 2030 World Cup.

It comes after Nagelsmann left the role following Germany's penalty shootout defeat to Paraguay in the round of 32 this summer.

Ahead of Klopp's appointment becoming official, his backroom team is now starting to take shape.



According to Sky Germany's Florian Plettenberg, Sven Bender is in talks to become his assistant.

Negotiations are said to be in the final stages but nothing has yet been signed.



The former Borussia Dortmund midfielder will be joined by two of Klopp's ex-Liverpool staff members on his coaching staff.

Both Peter Krawietz and Pep Lijnders are also expected to join the national team set-up.



Meanwhile, Per Mertesacker remains in talks to become the German FA's new managing director.

Familiar face

As a player, Bender made 181 appearances for Dortmund under Klopp during his fabled time as manager.

The pair won two Bundesliga titles and reached the 2013 Champions League final together.

4 Bender won two Bundesliga titles with Dortmund during Klopp's time as manager Credit: Shutterstock



Bender also lifted the DFB Pokal in 2012 as part of a league and cup double for Klopp's side.

Having won seven caps for Germany, the 37-year-old retired in the summer of 2024.

He has previously worked with the national team at youth level as well as a brief return to Dortmund as Edin Terzic's assistant.

Bender's most recent role saw him manage Unterhaching to a third place finish in the German fourth-tier last season.



Klopp's task

As for Klopp, he is set to take on his first coaching role since leaving Liverpool two years ago.

The 59-year-old has been Red Bull's head of global soccer since the start of last year, with his deal running until the end of 2029.

4 Bender won seven caps for Germany during his playing career Credit: News Group Newspapers Ltd

However, it is now understood he will be unveiled as Germany boss at a press conference in Frankfurt on Friday.



His first match in charge will come away to the Netherlands in September as the Nations League gets underway.

Germany will also face Greece and Serbia in the competition ahead of the start of Euro 2028 qualifying next year.

Klopp is set to be tasked with banishing the national team's recent major tournament woes.

Their early World Cup exit this summer extended a 12-year wait for a knockout victory at the finals.



Germany have not won a match during the knockout stage since beating Argentina in the 2014 final.

4 Germany have not won a World Cup knockout match since the 2014 final Credit: Getty

Although they did advance from the group stage for the first time in three World Cups, Nagelsmann's side once again failed to reach the last 16.

Their recent record at the Euros has not been much better, with a round of 16 defeat to England in 2021 before losing to Spain in the quarter-finals on home soil two years ago.

Sports.title: William Saliba opts against having surgery to cure chronic back pain after Arsenal star suffered worrying injury during France's World Cup campaign
Sports.content:
William Saliba opts against having surgery to cure chronic back pain after Arsenal star suffered worrying injury during France's World Cup campaign

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

William Saliba is believed to have opted not to undergo back surgery after suffering a worrying injury while on duty for France at the World Cup.

The Arsenal defender was captured saying 'my back is gone, my back is gone' after being withdrawn in the second-half of Les Bleus' defeat to Spain, with reports in his home country suggesting that he could be sidelined for an extended period of time.

But according to L'Equipe, the Premier League winner has since spoken to Arsenal's medical team, and instead chosen not to undergo surgery.

While this news could be seen as positive for Gunners fans, the French outlet did add that Saliba's injury will instead have a lengthy period of non-surgical treatment and rest, which could yet keep him out of the side for several months at the start of the season.

Saliba is set to keep track of the healing process to see how quickly it progresses however, which leaves a question mark over how long exactly Arsenal could be without their defensive stalwart.

Earlier in the tournament, the 25-year-old had previously revealed that he was managing a back injury as best as he could.

William Saliba will look to heal his chronic back pain without undergoing surgery, reports claim

'I've had some minor niggles for several months,' Saliba said. 'I've been gritting my teeth because there was the Champions League and the Premier League. But the coaching staff are handling it very well.

'The World Cup comes around only once every four years, so you've got to grit your teeth.

'I'm not at 100 per cent, but there are plenty of players who aren't at 100 per cent either. You can't make excuses.'

Saliba played 50 times in all competitions last season for Arsenal as the Gunners claimed the Premier League title and finished as Champions League and Carabao Cup runners-up.

He started France's opening two group stage matches at the World Cup, but was rested for their third after they qualified for the knock-out stages.

Saliba had played in each of France's knock-out matches until he was withdrawn in the second-half against eventual winners Spain, with Maxence Lacroix taking his place on the pitch first as a substitute, and then as a starter against England.

France's back line conceded a sensational four goals during the frantic first-half of the third-place play-off, and two in the second as England restored their commanding lead in the 6-4 bronze-medal match.

Sports.title: Lionel Messi's full humiliation laid bare: Left crying as his Argentine thugs disgraced themselves... how this World Cup exposed the GOAT's dark arts shame
Sports.content:
Lionel Messi's full humiliation laid bare: Left crying as his Argentine thugs disgraced themselves... how this World Cup exposed the GOAT's dark arts shame

Like so many sporting greats, Lionel Messi did not get the fairytale ending that his illustrious career deserved in New Jersey on Sunday night.

Throughout history it has proven a rarity for legendary athletes to exit the big stage on a high. Muhammad Ali lost three of his final four fights before hanging up his gloves. Michael Jordan bowed out from the NBA after failing to make the playoffs for a second straight year with the Washington Wizards. Tom Brady waved goodbye to football after a postseason loss to the Dallas Cowboys.

Babe Ruth, Roger Federer, Rafael Nadal... the list runs long. And now Messi's name has been added to it. Well, at least when it comes to the World Cup.

The sad sight of Argentina's icon shedding tears after their final defeat to Spain says it all. At 39, it is almost certain this was his closing chapter on soccer's grandest stage. He will be 43 when the next one rolls around.

Yet Messi didn't just sign off from the World Cup on the back of a loss. It was as miserable and shameful of a night as it could be for his country at MetLife Stadium.

After becoming the first finalists in history to fail to register a single shot in 90 minutes - and not testing Spain's goalkeeper Unai Simon once in 120 - Argentina's sore losers resorted to thuggery when Spain celebrated their triumph at full-time.

Lionel Messi did not get his fairytale ending as Argentina lost to Spain in the World Cup final

The Argentina icon exited the biggest stage in soccer on the most depressing of notes

Midfielder Leandro Paredes was the biggest villain, grabbing Spain's Eric Garcia by the neck and punching midfielder Gavi in the face before pushing him over. Defender Nahuel Molina also punched Rodri in the torso, while even a 53-year-old Argentine assistant coach landed a punch on Spain's Dani Olmo.

While he was not involved in the violence, Messi is captain of this team and what will likely prove his World Cup finale will always be remembered for the ugly scenes at full time.

The eight-time Ballon d'Or winner didn't cover himself in glory, either. In the wake of a red card for Argentina's Enzo Fernandez, Messi embarrassed himself with an attempt to send Marc Cucurella down the tunnel.

After Cucurella spoke to him while briefly covering his mouth, Messi stuck his arm in the air and signaled to the referee to try and get the Spain man sent off. FIFA's new rules forbid players from concealing conversations.

Fortunately, the official did not bow to the pressure of one of the game's finest ever players. But the sight of an all-time great, renowned for modesty on and off the field, resorting to dirty tactics was grim.

'One of the most pathetic things I've ever seen from a supposed sportsman,' Piers Morgan fumed on X about the incident. 'Messi's fake halo shattered in this World Cup; he was the sneaky cheating leader of a vile bunch of violent thugs.'

Once they'd grown tired of lashing out, the now-former world champions made it a masterclass in bitterness by refusing to form a guard of honor for Spain and turning their backs as their competitors lifted the World Cup.

They then sparked ugly scenes at full time by lashing out at Spain as they celebrated the win

Leandro Paredes grabbed Eric Garcia by the neck and punching Gavi before pushing him over

Messi also embarrassed himself with his desperate attempt to get Marc Cucurella sent off

Cucurella briefly touched his mouth while talking to Messi - players are sent off for covering their face while talking to opponents

The closing shot of Messi at a World Cup will forever be crying with his back to the trophy lift, surrounded by his henchmen, in a moment more befitting of 10-year-old children than elite athletes.

If that wasn't bad enough, Argentina skipped mandatory post-game media interviews and fled the stadium.

Messi is known for humility while cementing his status as arguably the greatest of all time, with the petulant antics of famous rival Cristiano Ronaldo - often accused of hogging the limelight and not being a good teammate - painting him in a better light.

Nevertheless, soccer's golden boy bid farewell to the World Cup with most wanting him to lose. He did exactly that, without managing a shot on target before Argentina disgraced themselves.

Other than fan footage of her leaving the stadium under the protection of burly security guards, there were also mysteriously few sightings of Messi's stunning wife, Antonela Roccuzzo, at Sunday's final.

It was a far cry from her usually-frequent appearances at the front of the stadium's VIP suites, cheering her man on alongside their children. How poignant, then, for her to be in hiding as Messi struggled and wept on a devastating day.

There were few sightings of Messi's wife, Antonela Roccuzzo, at the final other than her leaving

It took Antonela a day before she paid tribute to her husband on social media after the loss

She broke her silence a day later, writing on Instagram: 'You will always be the best. Thank you for showing us every day that true success is built through hard work, sacrifice, and perseverance - without ever losing sight of who you really are.

'You are the best example for our children and an inspiration to millions of people. I admire you more than words can express, and I feel immensely proud to walk through life by your side.'

All in all, it was an anticlimactic end for the Messi family at his sport's most prestigious competition.

Even his all-time World Cup goals record no longer remains. Less than a month after leapfrogging Germany icon Miroslav Klose in Argentina's second group-stage outing against Austria, France superstar Kylian Mbappe's brace in the third-place playoff took him one ahead of Messi on 21.

So what next? Messi has half the season to finish with Inter Miami, who return to action Wednesday after MLS's World Cup break.

But Messi won't play in their first game back against Chicago Fire, nor their trip to CF Montreal on Saturday.

According to ESPN, he'll also skip the MLS All-Star Game on July 29, too. It would be the third time Messi has been selected for the annual showpiece. He is yet to play in a single one.

A more likely return is Miami's clash with Columbus Crew on Saturday August 1.

Once back up and running at club level, Messi has over two years remaining on his current deal with the team, which extends beyond the 2028 Copa America.

Messi may stick around at club level for a while but he will surely retire from Argentina duty

When he's still operating at such a high level - he still scored eight World Cup goals this year - it would be a shock to see him end that contract early.

As for his international career, it remains to be seen whether Messi calls it a day after two consecutive World Cup final appearances. It would make most sense.

Prior to the final he hinted as such by referring to it as 'The Last Tango' in a post on social media. Following the defeat, he also shared an emotional message on Instagram which felt like a farewell.

'The pain is immense, and this wound will take time to heal,' he wrote. 'But I also hold onto all the good things.

'Thank you from the bottom of my heart for every greeting and message. Once again, we managed to unite as a country and stand together, sharing the immense pride of being Argentine.'

Presumably through gritted teeth, he added: 'I also want to congratulate Spain on winning the championship.'

If only he and Argentina could have done a better job of that on the field.

Sports.title: Arsenal transfer briefing: Why the Bruno Guimaraes deal could be hijacked, how Gunners found out about Morgan Rogers snub, the blow in Bradley Barcola chase, latest on Bournemouth duo and major William Saliba injury update
Sports.content:
Arsenal are effectively being told 'to put up or shut up' in their pursuit of Newcastle United midfielder Bruno Guimaraes.

All discussions so far have come from the Brazilian midfielder's agent and Newcastle are becoming increasingly agitated by what they view as a 'tactical process' with the player becoming distracted by the speculation over his future which is being played out in public.

Guimaraes has told Newcastle he wishes to talk to Arsenal and have the chance to win more titles but the club stance is he is not for sale.

Arsenal have been led to believe a deal for the 28-year-old can be achieved for around £75million but Newcastle would need more than that to be persuaded. They have had no formal offers from the Premier League champions and would point to the increasing market rate for midfielders.

The onus is firmly on sporting director Andrea Berta coming to the table with a proper offer.

Arsenal have been led to believe a deal for the 28-year-old Bruno Guimaraes can be achieved for around £75million but Newcastle would need more than that to be persuaded

How did Arsenal miss out on Rogers?

And there are other Premier League clubs circling around Guimaraes. That will sound all too familiar to Arsenal fans. It will stick in the craw to see Morgan Rogers declaring his delight at joining 'London's biggest club' ... Chelsea.

For a long period, Arsenal thought they were in pole position for Rogers, but they were led to believe £80m to £100m would be enough. Villa felt they weren't reading the market.

That became more apparent when Villa co-owner and chairman Nassef Sawiris had an informal chat with Arsenal in the USA and it was clear they were some distance apart in terms of their prices. Arsenal had their valuation in mind, despite Villa insisting on a record fee for a British player.

Arsenal were favourites for Rogers. As Daily Mail Sport reported, England team-mates Declan Rice and Bukayo Saka were part of a charm offensive. Martin Odegaard also spoke to Rogers, as did manager Mikel Arteta.

The 23-year-old was open to the move, even though a little typecast as a replacement for Leandro Trossard and Gabriel Martinelli, who is also for sale, as an option for the left wing. It just needed the right bid.

Yet when Arsenal failed to read the room, Chelsea seized their chance. The Blues began formal negotiations with Villa and Rogers’ representatives the day after England’s semi-final defeat by Argentina.

Reece James leaned on Rogers, Cole Palmer sent his best pal a text message and Arteta's old childhood friend, Xabi Alonso, phoned Rogers on Friday to explain his plans. Personal terms were agreed the same day. Chelsea agreed on £117m and Arsenal were informed. They decided their money could be spent better elsewhere.

Arsenal put on a charm offensive for Morgan Rogers (above) with Bukayo Saka, Declan Rice and Martin Odegaard all speaking to the player - but he ended up at Chelsea

Reece James (right) helped convince Rogers to move to Stamford Bridge

Now Rogers has gone, who are Arsenal after?

Atletico Madrid's Julian Alvarez remains a dream target. Though he is set on Barcelona, Arsenal would bid if they thought they had a chance.

Arsenal are also competing with Liverpool for Paris Saint-Germain's Bradley Barcola though the Anfield club are considered to have the upper hand at this stage.

Spain World Cup hero Ferran Torres has been suggested again as he considers leaving Barcelona, with PSG favourites. There are also rumblings Nico Williams could finally consider leaving Athletic Bilbao once he finishes his holiday.

'We need to stay calm; let him enjoy himself and disconnect from soccer. What is meant to happen will happen,' said his agent Felix Tainta helpfully.

All have been discussed. But the price has to be right.

The same applies to £85m-rated Eli Junior Kroupi at Bournemouth and his team-mate Alex Scott. Arsenal know from Chelsea's failed bid that it will take more than £64m to prise away the 22-year-old midfielder Scott this summer.

Lille's Ayyoub Bouaddi is now £85m when he was considered a £60m prospect before the World Cup. Manchester City are leading that chase.

Roma's Manu Kone is another Arsenal are briefed on. He would be more affordable if they proceed, though Manchester United are also around that deal.

Liverpool are beating Arsenal in the race for PSG and France star Bradley Barcola

Arsenal are keen on midfielder Alex Scott but know it is going to take a lot of money to get him out of Bournemouth

And the defence?

William Saliba has decided not to have surgery on his back injury after consultation with Arsenal. But the player will have a long period of rest and with the duration of that undetermined, but is likely to be three to four months so it is crucial they find suitable cover.

Free agent John Stones, another Chelsea and Inter Milan target, is on their list as is West Ham's versatile Aaron Wan-Bissaka - but not at £25m.

Maxence Lacroix was a player discussed briefly but is destined for Chelsea and Inter are reluctant to lose Jacobo Ramon.

Arsenal's recent enquiry for Villa defender Ezri Konsa showed the clubs were miles apart. The Gunners are of the understanding £30-35m is the England centre-back's value, Villa see it more like £60m. Konsa would like to join Arsenal but they know Villa's stance.

Real Madrid's Raul Asencio, now surplus at the Bernabeu, is another name to be floated.

In good news, at least Ben White is fit again and in no rush to depart. And as Daily Mail Sport revealed, Arsenal have also added highly-rated centre back Elijah Upson from neighbours Tottenham. Though compensation has still to be agreed for the 18-year-old son of former England defender Matthew, he could push himself into the first-team scene quickly.

Crystal Palace defender Maxence Lacroix was discussed by Arsenal briefly but he is destined for Chelsea

Arsenal and Aston Villa have very different ideas about the value of Ezri Konsa (right)

Any youngsters in Arsenal's sights?

Despite the disappointment of missing out to Manchester City in the race for 17-year-old winger Jeremy Monga, Arsenal are pushing to sign 16-year-old Crystal Palace striker Mylo Bernard. His contract expired last month, however, Palace have also offered improved terms.

Arsenal have spoken to Cardiff City too about Axel Donczew. The 16-year-old midfielder became the youngest player in Cardiff's history last season.

And who's heading for the exit?

Fulham have rekindled interest in winger Reiss Nelson who needs to find regular game time after a disappointing loan at Brentford. Benfica and Valencia are also in the mix.

Charles Sagoe Jr is wanted by AIK in Sweden and Hamburg continue to try and appease Arsenal with offers for Fabio Vieira.

Eric Huwer, Hamburg's chief financial officer, told German media yesterday: 'We fell a bit in love with Fabio Vieira last year. We feel like we’re fighting for him every single day. We’ve also backed up our interest with Arsenal with financial figures, but right now, no one is flinching.

'We’re confident we can make Fabio a very competitive offer within our means. We’re naturally very curious to see whether he and Arsenal will accept it.'

Indeed.

Sports.title: Inside Alejandro Garnacho's Chelsea exit: The game that sealed his fate, why Aston Villa target is happy to leave - and what Cobham insiders made of 'misunderstood' personality behind the scenes
Sports.content:
Inside Alejandro Garnacho's Chelsea exit: The game that sealed his fate, why Aston Villa target is happy to leave - and what Cobham insiders made of 'misunderstood' personality behind the scenes

Unlock more from Kieran Gill inside the Chelsea camp with a DailyMail+ subscription - brilliant exclusives, in-depth insight, analysis and more

Unai Emery had a front-row seat to see Alejandro Garnacho at his very best. The Aston Villa manager cut a frustrated figure in his technical area, watching while the winger reserved one of his finer performances for Chelsea in a 4-1 away victory at Villa Park in early March.

With Pedro Neto suspended, Garnacho exuded positivity throughout. Rarely did he seek to play a safe pass backwards. He was fast, direct, and unselfishly set up Joao Pedro to complete his hat-trick.

Our only gripe on the night was that Garnacho did not grab a goal for himself. He had enough opportunities while bursting beyond Emery’s back line.

Even so, Villa Park witnessed the potential of this player, who only turned 22 years old a few weeks back. There is an attacker who can influence games lying within, and if Villa are successful in signing Garnacho after opening talks with Chelsea over an initial loan with a conditional obligation to buy, perhaps Emery could be the coach to coax that confidence out of him.

Neither Enzo Maresca nor Liam Rosenior nor Calum McFarlane were able to do so during his single season with Chelsea. Electric evenings like that one at Villa were rare. Those at Stamford Bridge were more used to seeing Garnacho struggle for form on their left wing, and there was one Premier League game in particular which impacted how his campaign ended.

That was in late January, when Chelsea were losing at home to West Ham and Garnacho had given up possession 10 times by the 32nd minute. He was hooked at half-time while his team were trailing 2-0. In the second half, they staged a comeback, winning 3-2 without him.

Alejandro Garnacho's Chelsea career is all but over after just one disappointing season, with Aston Villa primed to sign him

Former Manchester United star Garnacho started just two of Chelsea's final 14 Premier League games in 2025-26

In the 14 Premier League fixtures which followed that turnaround, Garnacho started only twice – one of those arriving at Villa. Both club and player came to the conclusion that it was not working.

Indeed, sources on both sides today say the decision for Garnacho to leave is mutual. It is not only that Chelsea want to find Garnacho a new home. Garnacho wants out of Chelsea, too.

The 22-year-old Argentinian sensed his status as surplus to requirements. The final reminder came in the last game of the season away at Sunderland. Garnacho never received word to remove his orange bib.

He remained an unused substitute in a match the visitors only needed to avoid losing to secure some form of European football. They lost 2-1 at the Stadium of Light.

As revealed by Daily Mail Sport earlier this month, Garnacho did not return for pre-season at Cobham alongside all of their other non-World Cup call-ups. That followed talks between him and Chelsea. He was told he could stay away while they worked on securing a transfer.

Despite his disappointing season, there was belief inside the club that the market was aching for wingers like him. Chelsea were prioritising a permanent sale while speaking with Serie A side Roma, but then Villa came along, with Garnacho and Nicolas Jackson’s names raised during their talks for Morgan Rogers.

Villa do not mind taking a chance on a player who has encountered an unfortunate patch in his career. They did so with Marcus Rashford and Jadon Sancho. The only concern for Chelsea might be that Villa did not then sign either of those players permanently, and the same goes for Harvey Elliott, the Liverpool loanee who was practically held hostage by his own conditional obligation – of 10 appearances – last season.

Garnacho was only signed by Chelsea from Manchester United last summer. He turned down an approach from Saudi side Al Nassr in that window. There was also an enquiry from Bayern Munich before they signed Luis Diaz, and – as a reminder of Emery’s long-term respect – Villa. Chelsea paid a fixed fee worth £40million with no add-ons, and United retained a 10 per cent sell-on clause.

Chelsea tried to help Garnacho along the way. Liam Rosenior (left) felt a particular need to try to protect his player, sensing he was someone who preferred an arm around him

Garnacho celebrates after forcing an own goal from Arthur Okonkwo in Chelsea's FA Cup win at Wrexham in March - but positive moments were few and far between last term

Employees at Cobham were unsure what to expect with Garnacho. Like all of us, they had heard the stories, had seen how it ended at United, and were aware he arrived with a reputation.

Yet speak to those sources today and you will find they rather liked the lad. He is described as shy and misunderstood, and we are reminded that he arrived at Chelsea at the age of 21.

He also turned up later than everyone else, without a pre-season behind him, and ended up playing under three head coaches in nine months. It was not an easy campaign in which to adapt to a new club.

Chelsea tried to help Garnacho along the way. Rosenior felt a particular need to try to protect his player, sensing he was someone who preferred an arm around him.

When asked at one press conference why Garnacho was booed wherever he went, Rosenior’s answer bordered on what your mum tells you when the bullies at school are being mean – jealousy. ‘I don't understand why that happens,’ Rosenior told us. ‘Maybe it’s because he can be such a threat.’

Chelsea put their player up for a Champions League press conference before playing Atalanta. That presser was only the warm-up. The club then arranged a sit-down interview with Premier League Productions to tell his story and to his credit, Garnacho came across as sincere, or a ‘normal guy’ as he described himself.

He discussed being a humble father to his two-year-old son Enzo, and conceded he had made mistakes – presumably referring to his social media presence, like when he wore a Villa shirt with fellow outcast Marcus Rashford’s name on the back.

Now, he could be wearing a Villa shirt all over again, should talks lead to an agreement.

Aston Villa boss Unai Emery doesn't mind taking a chance on a player who has encountered an unfortunate patch in his career. He did so with Marcus Rashford (pictured)

Speak to those sources at Cobham and you will find they rather liked Garnacho. He is described as shy and misunderstood

It is naturally a curious link, given both Chelsea and Villa are working under financial restrictions with UEFA, who would scrutinise any deal struck for Garnacho so soon after Rogers headed in the other direction for £117m. They can bet other clubs will be watching what happens closely, too.

Per UEFA’s written rules, if a conditional obligation in a loan is considered to be ‘virtually certain’, then the temporary transfer must be categorised as a permanent one from the offset. It would need to be seen as genuinely conditional in the eyes of European football’s governing body.

Villa could, of course, argue that their loan arrangement for Elliott may have appeared ‘virtually certain’ – he only had to play 10 Premier League games to be bought permanently from Liverpool for £35m – but it was never triggered.

Whatever happens, Chelsea and Garnacho realise their time together is up, after a season in which they learned they were not suited for one another.

Sports.title: Roma attempt to hijack Al-Hilal's £60m move for West Ham star Crysencio Summerville with last-ditch swoop - as Issa Diop makes £8.5m Premier League switch: WINDOW WATCH
Sports.content:
It's that time of the year again - the transfer window is now open until September 1 and it's sure to be a busy period with clubs looking to make big signings ahead of next season.

Here are today's latest developments from Simon Jones and the Daily Mail Sport team...

Hull pushing to beat Ipswich for free agent Morita

Hull City have moved to try and beat Ipswich Town to the signing of Hidemasa Morita following his departure from Sporting Lisbon as a free agent.

Leeds United had also been in talks with the 31-year-old prior to the midfielder leaving the Portuguese side this summer.

Morita was a popular figure at Sporting, he played 31 times last season, and fans wanted him to stay but he now looks increasingly likely to join Premier League new boys Hull after their ambitious play to sign him.

Roma's last-gasp Summerville swoop

Roma have made a last ditch attempt to persuade Crysencio Summerville to choose them over Al-Hilal.

Roma have made a last ditch attempt to persuade Crysencio Summerville to sign for them

Coach Gian Piero Gasperini spoke to Summerville last night to try and convince him Roma's project was more suitable for the Netherlands international.

Al Hilal have agreed a £60m fee with West Ham with £55m up front.

Roma had offered £39m plus add ons.

The Italians are also keen on Chelsea defender Axel Disasi who was a teammate of Summerville's at West Ham last season.

They also made an offer for Chelsea's Alejandro Garnacho but Aston Villa's proposal for the winger offers more guarantees.

Wober departs Elland Road

Leeds United defender Maximilian Wober is joining Schalke on a free transfer.

The 28-year-old, who spent last season on loan at Werder Bremen, has been having a medical with Schalke.

Wober and Leeds are finalising a mutual agreement to terminate his contract a year early.

Valencia remain keen to sign Leeds attacking midfielder Largie Ramazani too.

Van Hecke completes Spurs move

Fellow Netherlands international Jan Paul van Hecke has now completed his £52million move to Tottenham from Brighton.

The Dutch centre-half, who chalked up three goals and three assists from 36 Premier League match for the Seagulls last term, had one year left on his contract at the Amex before Spurs swooped in to sign him.

It marks the latest signing in what has been a busy transfer window for Spurs, with Sandro Tonali, Mateus Fernandes, Andrew Robertson, Martin Dubravka and Marcos Senesi all joining Roberto De Zerbi's ranks ahead of the new season.

Meanwhile, Middlesbrough have confirmed the signing of striker Will Lankshear from Tottenham in a deal worth £20million including add-ons.

He has signed a five year contract and said: 'Middlesbrough is such a massive club over the years; I deem it to be a Premier League club.

'The project here really excites me. I can’t wait to get started and be part of the journey, and get this club back where it belongs.'

Lankshear scored 11 goals in 43 appearances for Oxford United last season and also had interest from Wolves.

Jan Paul van Hecke has now completed his £52million move to Tottenham from Brighton

Tigers see £13.6m Danois bid rejected

Hull City have had a £13.6million bid rejected for Auxerre midfielder Kevin Danois.

The 22-year-old, who is also on Newcastle United’s watchlist, has emerged as a top target for Hull but Auxerre value him closer to £25million.

That would require Hull to smash their club transfer record and they want at least two new midfielders.

Danois is a France U21 international and made 33 appearances in Ligue 1 last term, scoring three times and registering one assist.

Liverpool's swoop for Monaco star comes up short

Liverpool made an approach for Monaco attacking midfielder Maghnes Akliouche early in the window.

The club checked on the potential availability of the 24-year-old but it was evident he was a prime target for Paris Saint-Germain.

PSG have made offers to Monaco for the France international but have still to agree on the fee.

Liverpool did not progress with talks after their initial check and are exploring other options including PSG's Bradley Barcola.

Wolves outcast Arokodare poised for swift exit

Ajax have joined the clubs showing interest in Wolves' wantaway striker Tolu Arokodare.

Arokodare will not be part of Wolves' squad to face Maidenhead tonight after his actions prompted coach Cesar Peixoto to cancel training on Monday.

The Nigerian refused to exit the training pitch when asked prompting the session to be cancelled. Extra security was then called in to the training ground on Tuesday to ensure the 25-year-old striker did not disrupt the session again.

Arokodare, who joined from Genk last summer, has been frustrated that his proposed loan move to Torino has not developed while Genoa have also made an enquiry.

Arokodare did not initially travel with the squad for last week’s warm weather training camp in Portugal, only receiving a late call-up following an injury to fellow forward Adam Armstrong.

In April, he faced disciplinary action after a dressing room bust-up with team-mate Mateus Mane during a 4-0 defeat at West Ham.

Wolves cancelled training after wantaway striker Tolu Arokodare refused to leave the pitch

Diop makes Premier League switch

Ipswich Town have confirmed the signing of Issa Diop from Fulham in a deal worth around £8.5m.

The centre-back has signed a four-year deal.

Ipswich schedule medical

Ipswich have also scheduled a medical for this week ahead of completing the £10million signing of Daizen Maeda from Celtic.

Ipswich agreed a deal for the forward worth an initial £8m plus £2m in add-ons.

Talks are continuing over a deal for free agent midfielder Hidemasa Morita, formerly of Sporting Lisbon, as well as Union SG’s Dutch goalkeeper Kjell Scherpen.
