World.title: EIS uses €6.5 million communications budget to target 20 countries
World.content:
Ursel Velve, head of the Estonian Business and Innovation Agency (EIS), says the agency aims to justify every euro of its communications budget, calling the spending essential for promoting Estonia abroad.

When Velve took over leadership of EIS about a year ago, she examined the foundation's marketing and communication activities in detail. Previously, each EIS department had its own marketing and communication team, and when information about all their activities was compiled, the list contained about three hundred items.

EIS merged these teams, and at the beginning of 2026 the number of employees there was reduced from 70 to 39. "We have critically reviewed all the activities we do and all the people, so that everyone contributes to the maximum," Velve said.

Velve said that when she started, she questioned above all those EIS communication expenses related to conferences or events aimed at small groups — events similar to those organized by the private sector — where costs were quite high while the value gained for the state was questionable.

Although public‑sector institutions employ a large number of communication staff, the state is paying increasingly large sums to private PR firms. EIS is among the biggest user of PR firms, despite having 39 employees working in marketing and communication.

According to Velve, the EIS communication budget this year is 6.5 million euros, divided across 20 countries in five fields: export, investment, growth of the start‑up community, e‑residency and tourism. Therefore, Velve noted, the amount per country and field is very small.

She gave an example from her previous experience working at a large electronics company, where the marketing and communication budget was about 2 percent of turnover — 3 million euros per year. "If a single product‑group company in small Estonia markets with 3 million, then our 6.5 million to make Estonia visible globally is still a very small amount."

She said that of the 39‑member EIS communication and marketing team, only three work on domestic communication, while the rest work outward toward 20 countries.

"The issue is that there are not many specialists or agencies in Estonia that truly have a strong international contact network in foreign markets. For example, last year we helped the EIS carry out a project aimed at supporting Estonian companies in export markets. To do such work, you need knowledge, experience and contacts in countries such as South Korea, the United States, Japan, Germany and many others," said Miltton New Nordics CEO Annika Arras.

"If we consider that we have large countries — the United Kingdom, Germany, Finland, Sweden, Singapore, South Korea and others — then inevitably each country has its own cultural differences and channels. On our own we simply cannot grasp what is most effective in a specific country," Velve explained.

Therefore, local partners must be involved.

"For example, there was a defense‑industry fair in Poland, where we took Estonian companies. Before and after the fair we did a lot of communication, which resulted in a defense‑industry media trip to Estonia that brought us 23 million contacts through coverage. Through this, cooperation between Estonian and Polish defense‑industry companies significantly intensified," Velve noted. "On one hand, the sums may seem large, but considering what it brings back to Estonia, it is certainly a worthwhile investment."

EIS has discussed with Estonian ministries, the Government Office and business associations how to organize Estonia's international marketing, and everyone says that marketing Estonia is extremely important, Velve said. "No one else in Estonia does it, so EIS must continue."

EIS is also involved, together with the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and the Ministry of Economic Affairs and Communications, in organizing 2027 Ukraine reconstruction conference in Tallinn. "There we need good project‑based people who can bring defense‑industry companies from across the Nordic region to Estonia."

World.title: US dollar rises against Iraqi dinar
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The exchange rate for the US dollar compared to the Iraqi dinar rose on Wednesday in the Iraqi capital, Baghdad, and the capital of the Kurdistan region of Iraq, Erbil.

The US dollar exchange rate slightly rose in Baghdad’s al-Kifah and al-Harithiya stock exchanges, reaching 1,504 Iraqi dinars compared to 1,502.5 Iraqi dinars on Wednesday’s morning.

The exchange rate in currency exchange shops in Baghdad ranged between 1,510 Iraqi dinars and 1,500 Iraqi dinars, Shafaq News reported.

In Erbil, the US dollar exchange rate also rose, fluctuating between 1,508.5 and 1,507.5 Iraqi dinars.

The Central Bank of Iraq (CBI) said in February 2023 that it has begun using the new US dollar exchange rate of 1,300 dinars to every US dollar.

The previous official exchange rate was 1,450 dinars to one US dollar, which was being exchanged in the parallel market at a rate of 1,550 dinars.

While the official exchange rate was 1,450 dinars per dollar in January 2023, the US currency was being exchanged at 1,610 dinars during the same month in the parallel market in Iraq. This variation indicated a difference of over 10 percent in the exchange rates.

World.title: PM Al Zaidi proposes joint fund in call with German Chancellor Friedrich Merz
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — Prime Minister Ali Falih al-Zaidi held high-level telephone discussions with German Chancellor Friedrich Merz on Wednesday, July 22, 2026, focusing on expanding economic cooperation, trade, and industrial investment between the two nations.

According to an official statement released by the Prime Minister’s Media Office, the talks covered bilateral ties across multiple sectors, with particular emphasis on economic partnerships, trade volume expansion, direct investment, and joint migration management frameworks.

Key Discussion Pillars

Joint Iraqi-German Fund: Prime Minister Al-Zaidi proposed establishing a dedicated joint fund to finance industrial development projects in Iraq with German technical and capital backing.

Economic Reforms & Anti-Corruption: Al-Zaidi reiterated Baghdad’s commitment to eradicating administrative corruption and creating an open, transparent environment for foreign capital to diversify Iraq’s national economy.

Official Invitation to Berlin: Chancellor Merz extended a formal invitation to Prime Minister Al-Zaidi to visit Germany for an official state visit to deepen economic and political coordination.

Support for Fiscal Reform: Germany reaffirmed its support for the Iraqi government’s ongoing economic and financial reforms, expressing strong readiness from German corporations to expand investment footprints across Iraq.

The discussions highlight Baghdad’s broader diplomatic strategy of leveraging European economic integration to modernize domestic industrial infrastructure and broaden trade partnerships beyond energy exports.

World.title: Lebanon PM says Beirut working for ‘complete Israeli withdrawal’
World.content:
Zawtar al-Gharbiyah – Lebanon is working towards a “complete Israeli withdrawal” from areas it occupies, Prime Minister Nawaf Salam said on Wednesday on a visit to a village where Lebanon’s army recently deployed.

“We will continue mobilising our political and diplomatic efforts to secure a complete Israeli withdrawal from the south,” he said in Zawtar al-Gharbiya.

Israeli forces were previously present on the outskirts of the village following the war with Iran-backed Hezbollah.

Salam visited the town a day after Lebanese President Joseph Aoun met with his US counterpart Donald Trump at the White House, where he “stressed the urgent need for a full Israeli withdrawal from Lebanese territory”.

Under a US-sponsored agreement signed last month, Lebanon’s army is meant to disarm Hezbollah and the Israeli military is to withdraw from “pilot zones” where Lebanese forces will subsequently deploy.

Hezbollah has repeatedly rejected the agreement and refuses to lay down its weapons.

The military said on Tuesday that Israeli forces “opened fire” near troops deploying at Zawtar al-Gharbiya.

The Israeli military said it had only fired “warning shots into the air” after Lebanese soldiers entered an area that was “not part of the pilot area”.

Hezbollah drew Lebanon into the Middle East war by attacking Israel in support of Tehran on March 2, prompting major Israeli airstrikes and a ground invasion.

After planting a Lebanese flag in Zawtar al-Gharbiya on Wednesday, Salam said “in parallel with the army’s deployment, we will continue opening roads, removing rubble, and securing essential services, enabling our people to return safely and with dignity to their homes and villages”.

– ‘Heads held high’ –

The war caused widespread destruction, mainly in the south, though violence has declined since the signing of a framework agreement between the United States and Iran last month and the Lebanon-Israel deal.

According to the United Nations, more than 700,000 people have returned to their homes over the past few weeks.

In Zawtar al-Gharbiya, dozens of residents waited at the village’s entrance for permission to go check on their homes.

“We will enter the town with our heads held high, thanks to the presence of the Lebanese army,” Abbas Yaghi, 73, told AFP.

The military had told residents on Tuesday to avoid entering the village “until the security situation stabilises”.

The army is conducting a sweep of the town, which is geographically contiguous with its Israeli-occupied neighbour, Zawtar al-Shariqya.

Israeli troops still launch intermittent strikes in surrounding towns, the latest on Nabatieh al-Fawqa.

“We will follow the army if it gives us permission to enter,” Mostapha Ammar, a 60-year-old resident of Zawtar al-Sharqiya said, hoping that Israel would withdraw from other areas.

Wafaa Ismail, 64, also from Zawtar al-Sharqiya, was not granted permission to enter the neighbouring village as Salam visited.

She expressed frustration at seeing the prime minister enter on his own, escorted by the army, saying: “He should have brought the people in with him so he could claim victory.”

World.title: Ukraine’s new army chief: who is Mykhailo Drapaty?
World.content:
Kyiv – Ukrainian leader Volodymyr Zelensky has announced Mykhailo Drapaty as the country’s new commander-in-chief, following a political crisis triggered by Zelensky’s surprise ousting of a young modernising defence minister.

The 43-year-old Drapaty replaces Oleksandr Syrsky, 60, an accomplished military strategist but who was long criticised for Soviet-style practices and not caring about human losses.

Here is what we know about Drapaty.

– Fighting Russian separatists –

Drapaty is a career military officer trained exclusively inside Ukraine’s independent, post-Soviet system.

He began as a lieutenant and rose through the ranks, shooting to nationwide fame during the war with Russia-backed separatists in 2014.

In a video which went viral, he commanded an infantry vehicle as it smashed through a makeshift barricade set up by pro-Moscow forces in the southern city of Mariupol.

Recalling the incident in an interview with Ukrainian media, Drapaty said his driver asked: “Major, there are barricades ahead. What do we do?”

“I said, ‘Dima, step on the gas'”.

The vehicle, with the blue-and-yellow Ukrainian flag affixed to its top, then smashes through the tyre-and-barricade wall, leaping into the air and speeding on.

During the fight with Moscow-backed rebels, Drapaty is also credited with re-capturing several settlements from Russian control and then saving his unit from being encircled.

Drapaty has a wife and kids, Ukrainian media reported.

– Backing army ‘transformation’ –

Drapaty is seen as a consensus candidate and popular choice.

He enjoys a good reputation within the military, and protesters calling for his predecessor’s removal often chanted his name as their preferred replacement.

Despite being well-known, he has kept a low profile and only rarely given interviews — in contrast with many other Ukrainian commanders.

After a string of Russian attacks on Ukrainian training grounds, he resigned from his position as ground forces commander in June 2025 — a move that set him apart as commander willing to take responsibility for mistakes.

“If we fail to draw conclusions, to change our attitude toward service, to acknowledge our mistakes, we are doomed,” he said at the time.

“That episode illustrates his decisiveness and strong ethical standards,” political commentator Volodymyr Fesenko told AFP on Wednesday.

Drapaty was immediately moved to become head of Ukraine’s joint forces command, from where he pushed for reforms inside the system.

After the dismissal of moderniser Fedorov last week, he said the “transformation” of the army must continue.

“When the right decision has to be implemented in spite of the system, rather than because of it, it means that the system itself needs to change,” he said in a rare public intervention.

“The army needs new rules,” he added.

– Hailed as ‘fresh air’ –

His nomination was hailed by many inside and outside the army.

The appointment is “wonderful news”, said Sergiy Prytula, the head of one of Ukraine’s biggest charities supporting the military.

“This is a breath of fresh air and a new hope in the struggle of free people for freedom and justice,” the ousted defence minister Fedorov, an ally, said on social media.

In Moscow, Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said the change would not impact the course of the war.

“I don’t think this will lead to any changes on the front lines,” he told reporters, adding that Moscow intends to continue pressing on with its almost four-and-a-half-year offensive.

– Facing a ‘very difficult time’ –

Despite Ukraine being in one of its best positions on the front line in months, Drapaty faces serious challenges.

The army has been blighted by several scandals — particularly over an unpopular mobilisation drive, the treatment of conscripts and reports of widespread absenteeism and equipment shortages in some units.

“The new Commander-in-Chief of the Armed Forces of Ukraine will have a very difficult time. Much harder than he imagines,” former army chief Valery Zaluzhny — removed in 2024 — said.

The public row over the last week has exposed hidden divisions within Ukraine’s military and political leadership.

His appointment, seen as an attempt to bridge the divide, carries heavy expectations.

“Appointments made against a backdrop of social turmoil always come with many pitfalls,” said Prytula, adding that Drapaty now faces “inflated expectations”.

World.title: Iraq signs $200 billion in deals with US energy companies
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Oil Minister Basim Khudair said on Tuesday that the deals struck with US energy corporations during Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi’s visit to the United States are estimated at $200 billion.

In a televised interview, Khudair explained that the new agreements will raise Iraq’s oil production capacity, create job opportunities, and help the country achieve self-sufficiency in gas by 2030, according to the Iraqi News Agency (INA).

The deals include agreements with HKN Energy, Chevron, and Halliburton to develop the oilfields of Hamrin, West Qurna-2, Nasiriyah, Balad, Bin Omar, and Sindbad, as well as an agreement with Syria to construct the Haditha-Baniyas oil pipeline.

Khudair noted that Iraq’s current oil production capacity is 4.8 million barrels per day, but the government is in serious discussions with the Organization of Petroleum Exporting Countries (OPEC) to increase oil exports.

Just like most other oil producers, Iraq has to face the issue of how to attract investments and increase production under the restrictions imposed by OPEC.

Despite having some of the world’s greatest crude oil reserves, ongoing production constraints impede Iraq’s efforts to generate revenues needed to support its growing population.

World.title: Italian FA chief says in touch with Guardiola over coaching vacancy
World.content:
Rome – The head of Italy’s football federation has confirmed he held discussions with legendary coach Pep Guardiola over the vacancy at the Italian national side but added he was “not sure that this will come about”.

Giovanni Malago revealed the talks had taken place in an interview with the website Cronache di Spogliatoio (Dressing Room Chronicles) published on Wednesday.

Asked whether the budget for the coach’s salary could be increased in the case of Guardiola, he said: “Yes, and that is the exception for obvious reasons”.

“I won’t go into detail here but it’s not sure that this will come about.

“However, I still believe it was the right thing to do. It was important to open a dialogue and keep it alive,” he added.

Guardiola has first hand knowledge of Italian football having played for Brescia and AS Roma (2001-03).

Already at a low ebb, Italian football was sent into a tailspin in March after the men’s national team failed for a third consecutive time to qualify for the World Cup.

Italy has won four World Cups.

Guardiola, 55, stepped down at Manchester City at the end of last season after winning six Premier League titles and the Champions League in his glittering decade at the Etihad Stadium.

According to Italian media reports, former Italy internationals Andrea Pirlo and Roberto Mancini — who guided the Azzurri to the Euro 2020 title — are also being considered as candidates to coach the national team, which faces Belgium on September 25 in the Nations League.

World.title: Cooler inflation hands new UK PM Burnham an early boost
World.content:
London – Britain’s annual inflation rate fell more than expected in June, driven by lower fuel prices, official data showed Wednesday, in a boost to new Prime Minister Andy Burnham’s cost-of-living push.

The Consumer Prices Index rose by 2.6 percent in the 12 months to June, down from 2.8 percent in May, the Office for National Statistics said in a statement.

Analysts’ consensus forecast had been for a slowdown to 2.7 percent last month.

Much of the fall was a result of petrol and diesel prices easing as crude prices tumbled in the wake of a ceasefire between the United States and Iran.

However, analysts expect the inflation dip to be short-lived as fresh fighting in the Middle East this month led to the collapse of a preliminary peace deal, pushing oil prices back up.

Burnham, who became prime minister on Monday, has pledged to ease cost-of-living pressures, unveiling a tax cut on household electricity prices and a £2 ($2.70) cap on single bus fares in his first days in the job.

“Falling inflation is news families want to hear but there is much more to do to give people the breathing space they need,” said newly appointed finance minister John Healey.

“We have chosen to focus on the cost of living in our first week, signalling that concern for working people will be at the heart of everything we do,” he added.

– ‘Higher inflation still coming’ –

Burnham announced that value-added tax (VAT) would be taken off electricity bills from October in a policy costing the Labour government about £850 million in the current UK financial year.

The measure’s start date coincides with an expected rise in the UK energy regulator’s price cap on electricity and gas bills, a consequence of the ongoing US-Iran war that will likely spur inflation.

“Higher inflation is still coming,” said Paul Dales, chief UK economist at Capital Economics.

“The lagged effect from high energy prices will probably lift inflation above 3.0 percent in September and to about 3.5 percent early next year,” he said.

Higher inflation meanwhile risks hikes to UK interest rates, analysts said.

The new PM has said he wishes to ease pressure also on small businesses, hit by the previous Labour administration’s tax hikes.

At the same time, Burnham has pledged to respect the strict fiscal discipline seen under his predecessor Keir Starmer, whereby the government balances tax receipts with day-to-day state spending.

Official data Tuesday showed UK government borrowing dropped more than expected in June, handing a boost Healey, who replaced Rachel Reeves as chancellor of the exchequer.

“While the general trend in the data is encouraging… the latest flare up in US-Iran tensions and the spike in oil prices means that it is unlikely to last, regardless of the cost-of-living measures deployed by the Burnham administration,” said Matthew Ryan, head of market strategy at Ebury.

Burnham’s long-term goal is a “reindustrialisation” of Britain and mass building of municipal housing.

World.title: Iraq Oil Minister: $200B U.S. energy deals to boost crude output and gas by 2030
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — Iraq’s Minister of Oil, Basim Mohammed Khudair, announced on Tuesday that the federal government is advancing a clear strategic roadmap to comprehensively expand the nation’s energy infrastructure.

Speaking during an interview on the official Al-Iraqiya News channel, the Minister confirmed that the agreements finalized during Prime Minister Ali Falih al-Zaidi’s official visit to Washington will significantly boost total crude reserves, increase daily production, and generate extensive employment and technical training opportunities across the country.

Khudair revealed that the total estimated value of the energy contracts, strategic agreements, and memorandums of understanding executed during the U.S. summit reaches approximately $200 billion, emphasizing that the active presence of top American energy firms sends a strong message of market confidence to international investors.

Key Highlights from the Washington Energy Portfolio

HKN Energy Deal: Strategic development agreement signed to expand production at the Hamrin oil field.

Chevron Expansion: Operations and development agreements covering West Qurna 2, as well as the Nasiriya and Balad fields.

Halliburton Integrated Management: Comprehensive field management pacts secured for the Bin Umar and Sindibad fields.

Syrian Export Corridor: A major cross-border pipeline agreement signed with Syria to construct and reactivate the strategic Haditha–Baniyas pipeline.

The Minister underscored that Iraq’s total crude oil production capacity has now officially crossed 4.8 million barrels per day (bpd). In response to severe disruptions caused by the closure of the Strait of Hormuz, Baghdad is actively establishing alternative export bypasses through both the Ceyhan pipeline to Turkey and the Baniyas route through Syria.

World.title: 'Responsibility of govt & opposition to protect children's future': Centre urges dialogue as protests intensify - top developments
World.content:
'Responsibility of govt & opposition to protect children's future': Centre urges dialogue as protests intensify

Here are the top developments throughout the day:

Opposition stages 'Black Day' protest in Parliament

Government offers Parliament discussion; opposition refuses without Pradhan's resignation



Rahul Gandhi attacks Centre, demands Pradhan's resignation



Supreme Court declines urgent hearing



Delhi high court seeks replies, orders CCTV footage preserved

CJP protests continue; Centre deploys more CRPF companies

CJP says it is ready for talks

Opposition MPs blocked from meeting Sonam Wangchuk

Wangchuk sets conditions for ending hunger strike

Wangchuk releases fresh video message

Nadda challenges Rahul's paper leak claims, urges Parliament debate

NEW DELHI: A political showdown over the alleged NEET paper leak and police action against student protesters intensified on Wednesday, with Parliament witnessing repeated disruptions, the Opposition staging a 'Black Day' protest, Rahul Gandhi renewing his attack on the Centre and activist Sonam Wangchuk extending his indefinite hunger strike.The Centre maintained that it was ready for a discussion on the issue in Parliament, but the opposition remained firm on its demand for Union education minister Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation.Hitting back at Rahul Gandhi's allegations, Union minister JP Nadda said the government would investigate his claims of around 150 paper leaks and urged the opposition to stop âchanging the goalpostâ and participate in a parliamentary debate to find a lasting solution.Meanwhile, the Delhi high court sought responses over allegations of police brutality during the students' protest, while the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) continued its agitation at Delhi's Jantar Mantar.Leader of opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi, along with INDIA bloc MPs, arrived in Parliament dressed in black to mark a âBlack Dayâ over the alleged NEET irregularities and the police action against protesting students.Congress MP Priyanka Gandhi Vadra, Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav, Trinamool Congress MP Mahua Moitra, JMM MP Mahua Maji and several other opposition leaders gathered at Makar Dwar, raising slogans demanding justice for students and the resignation of Union education minister Dharmendra Pradhan.Amid escalating protests, Parliamentary affairs minister Kiren Rijiju said the government was ready to debate the NEET issue in Parliament."The government is ready to hold a discussion on the NEET paper leak issue," Rijiju said, adding that an all-party meeting had been proposed to finalise the date, rule and duration of the debate."There should be a constructive discussion for the future of the youth of this country," he said.However, the opposition maintained that no discussion could take place unless Dharmendra Pradhan resigned.In the Rajya Sabha, Kharge reiterated that the minister must step down before any debate begins, while insisting on a discussion under Rule 267.Leader of the House JP Nadda accused the INDIA bloc of displaying âirresponsible behaviourâ and damaging Parliament's dignity.Addressing a press conference, Rahul Gandhi accused the government of destroying India's education system and backed students' demands in full.He claimed the country's education system had become âa rigged systemâ and alleged that there had been 152 paper leaks in the last decade without a single conviction."The thing that is very clear to everybody is that our education system, which was known to be one of the best education systems in the world, is today a rigged system," he said.He alleged that students were being forced to repeatedly prepare for examinations because of leaks."What we do know is that 152 paper leaks have taken place over the last decade. So, approximately one a month."Rahul also criticised police action against protesters."The question is, why is this happening to our students? What exactly have our students done?... They're protesting peacefully."Calling students' demands â100 per cent legitimateâ, he said: "Dharmendra Pradhan, who has failed as an education minister and is known to be corrupt, should be relieved of his duties."The Supreme Court declined an urgent hearing on a petition alleging police brutality during Monday's protest.When the petitioner's counsel referred to video evidence, Chief Justice of India Surya Kant remarked: "We are not interested in videos, we don't have time to watch."The petition concerns police action during the CJP's âSansad Chaloâ march, where protesters alleged excessive force by security personnel.The Delhi high court sought responses from the Centre, Delhi Police and the National Human Rights Commission on petitions alleging excessive force during the July 20 protest.A bench headed by Chief Justice DK Upadhyaya directed authorities to preserve CCTV footage, body camera recordings and all relevant electronic records.The court listed the matter for September 11.Petitioners alleged that police and the Rapid Action Force used disproportionate force against peaceful protesters, including women and children.Senior advocate N Hariharan claimed more than 90 students were injured and sought a judicial inquiry and an independent SIT probe.Additional Solicitor General SV Raju argued that the petitions relied on social media posts and maintained that protesters had turned violent, resulting in injuries to police personnel and damage to government vehicles.CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke criticised the government's decision to deploy 20 additional CRPF companies in Delhi."What is the government planning to do? Was the students' blood spilled by the Delhi Police and RAF on 20 July not enough?" he posted on X.The additional CRPF companies are being airlifted from West Bengal to strengthen security amid the ongoing protests and Parliament session.The CJP claimed thousands continued to gather at Jantar Mantar as the agitation entered its second month.The organisation reiterated that its protest would continue until Dharmendra Pradhan resigns.Dipke also clarified that the CJP had not called for protests anywhere other than Jantar Mantar and warned against "goons" attempting to create disturbances elsewhere.The CJP said it was open to discussions with the government but insisted any talks must take place at Jantar Mantar rather than at a minister's residence.Chief spokesperson Saurav Das said police had conveyed that Union minister JP Nadda wanted to meet them."We refused to go to anyone's house or office. The people's court is here," he said.A delegation of opposition MPs was stopped by police from meeting activist Sonam Wangchuk at Medanta Hospital in Gurugram.The MPs handed over a letter, signed by around 55 lawmakers, to Wangchuk's wife Gitanjali Angmo urging him to end his fast.AAP MP Sanjay Singh accused the Centre of âtyrannyâ, alleging that Union ministers were allowed to meet Wangchuk while opposition MPs were denied access.âFor the first time in history, you've heard that police are preventing people from meeting a hospitalized patient. We've come to meet Sonam Wangchuk, who is hospitalized, and why? 55 five MPs have signed this letter and after signing it, we've brought a letter requesting you to break his hunger strike. Do these people want to kill Sonam Wangchuk? This letter states that you should break your fast. Considering your health and the importance of your life, you should not continue your fast. Sonam Wangchuk had said that if the country's MPs reassure us, he can break his fast. We're not allowed to deliver this letter, not allowed to meet him... JP Nadda and Jitendra Singh met him and so many MPs from the opposition have come yet they will not let them meet him,â he said.Wangchuk, who has completed 25 days of his indefinite fast, said he would end it only if the government assured that no student protester would face legal action.In a letter to Union ministers JP Nadda and Jitendra Singh, he thanked them for visiting him but sought an unequivocal assurance."I respectfully request an unequivocal assurance from the Government that none of the young protesters will face any punitive or retaliatory legal action."He said if such an assurance was given, he would end his fast immediately.His wife, Gitanjali Angmo, later said Wangchuk had decided to continue the fast until such assurances were received.âSonam Wangchuk has decided to break his fast after receiving assurances and letters from these MPs. But he also needs assurances from the Government of India that no injustice will be done to the protesters. He also needs assurances from the government that they won't be physically assaulted tonight. Sonam has written this letter to Jitendra ji and Nadda ji, saying that he needs assurances that nothing wrong will be done to the children. No FIR will be filed against them, there will be no undue force against them... We are waiting for another assurance from the Government of India. Sonam has also tweeted today and has also written a letter to them that he wants assurance about the children because if we are doing this entire movement for the children and their future, then it is our responsibility not to cause any harm to them. Sonam has decided to extend his hunger strike indefinitely,â she said.In a video message from hospital, Wangchuk said he had lost around 11 kilograms during his hunger strike but remained determined.He praised students for maintaining restraint despite police action."I want to salute all the students who conducted themselves with remarkable restraint."He reiterated that he wanted to end the fast but would do so only after receiving assurances that students would not face police action, FIRs or legal harassment."If I receive that assurance soon... I will end my hunger strike today itself. But if no such assurance is given, then unfortunately I will have to continue my fast."JP Nadda hit back at Rahul Gandhi over his claim that around 150 paper leaks had taken place in the country, saying the matter would be investigated and the government would place the facts before the nation.Referring to Rahul Gandhi's press conference, Nadda said, "Leader of the Opposition Rahul Gandhi gave a presentation and discussed approximately 150 paper leaks. This is a matter of investigation, and the government, being a responsible government, will undoubtedly investigate and present the truth to the public and the nation."Reiterating the Centre's stand, Nadda said the government was ready for a discussion on the alleged NEET paper leak in Parliament under any format and for any duration decided by the Opposition."We have wanted this issue to be discussed in Parliament. Whether it is a short-duration discussion or a long-duration discussion, you decide how much time you want. The government is ready for discussion, and the Opposition should not keep changing the goalpost," he said.Calling Parliament the appropriate forum to address the issue, Nadda urged all parties to work together for a long-term solution."Children are ours, yours, and the future of the country. It is the responsibility of both the government and the Opposition to protect their future. We should discuss every aspect and come up with a concrete policy," he said.

World.title: Watch: TMC MLA Kunal Ghosh marshalled out, suspended after assembly ruckus
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Trinamool Congress (TMC) MLA Kunal Ghosh was suspended from the West Bengal Assembly for the remainder of Wednesday after he disrupted proceedings by interrupting rebel TMC Chief Whip Akhruzzaman during a debate on the Home and Hill Affairs budget.

The suspension came after marshals forcibly escorted Ghosh out of the House when he refused to return to his seat despite repeated directions from the Speaker.

The dramatic scenes unfolded amid an escalating power struggle between rival factions within the TMC legislature party.

Marshals remove Ghosh after disruption in House

The disruption began when Akhruzzaman, who belongs to the Ritabrata Banerjee-led rebel faction of the TMC, rose to speak during the debate.

Ghosh walked up to the microphone and interrupted him, questioning why his own name had allegedly been removed from the list of speakers.

Speaker Rathindra Bose repeatedly appealed to Ghosh to return to his seat, while senior leaders also attempted to defuse the situation.

However, after Ghosh refused to comply, the Speaker ordered Assembly marshals to remove him from the House. Ghosh resisted, leading to a brief scuffle before marshals carried him out, triggering protests inside the Assembly.





Industries minister Tapas Roy initially proposed that Ghosh be suspended for the remainder of the ongoing Assembly session. However, chief minister Suvendu Adhikari suggested that suspending him for the day would be sufficient.

"This type of behaviour is not acceptable. We are also in an opposition post, but there is some responsibility. Akhruzzaman is a senior MLA and his father was also a long-time MLA," Adhikari said.

The Speaker subsequently placed the proposal before the House, and Ghosh was suspended for the rest of the day through a voice vote, with support from BJP legislators as well as members of the rebel TMC faction.

Internal TMC rift spills onto Assembly floor

The incident highlighted the deepening divide between the Mamata Banerjee-led 'Kalighat' faction, to which Ghosh belongs, and the Ritabrata Banerjee-led rebel camp within the TMC legislature party.

Ghosh alleged that his name had been removed from the list of speakers despite being nominated to participate in the debate on the Home and Hill Affairs budget.

He claimed the move prompted his protest inside the House.

The confrontation comes a day after disagreements over the Opposition's list of speakers exposed tensions within the TMC legislature party.

Legislators aligned with the Kalighat faction had alleged that names recommended by them were being dropped from the speaking list, reflecting an ongoing battle over floor coordination and control within the party.

Assembly proceedings resumed only after Ghosh was removed from the House.

World.title: 'NEET paper leaked thrice in last 5 years': Annamalai lambasts former party BJP
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Former BJP leader K Annamalai on Wednesday criticised the Centre over its handling of the NEET controversy, alleging a lack of accountability despite repeated question paper leaks and questioning the delay in engaging with protesting students.

The former Tamil Nadu BJP chief, who now heads the "We the Leaders" movement and is set to launch his own political party, said the government should have initiated talks before the protests escalated.

"Why was meaningful engagement delayed until the protest had escalated to a flashpoint? What kept you waiting?" Annamalai asked in a statement.

Reiterating that protest is a fundamental right in a democracy, he urged the Centre to engage in meaningful dialogue, ensure transparency and take swift action to address students' concerns.

Annamalai said he had consistently supported NEET, arguing that it created a uniform admission process and offered students from underprivileged backgrounds a fair opportunity to pursue medical education.

However, he said the system had lost credibility after the NEET-UG question paper was allegedly leaked three times in the past five years.

"Imagine the amount of pressure it puts on students, who had to go through the examination process yet another time when the system that was supposed to bring in uniformity was failing," he said.





Alleging there had been "no accountability" for the repeated leaks, Annamalai said the failure of the examination system pushed students onto the streets.

"I believe strongly that it was that moment that brought in a shift in the minds of the students to take to the streets to cry their hearts out," he said.

Stressing that a nation's strength depends on the confidence its youth have in public institutions, Annamalai warned that the education system risks losing credibility if students no longer trust its fairness.

"If our students lose faith in the fairness and credibility of our education system, we are jeopardising the future of our nation," he said.

At the same time, Annamalai urged students and protest organisers to remain focused on their original demands, cautioning that prolonged agitations often attract people with vested interests seeking to divert the movement for political or unrelated agendas.

"If you remain silent and let these people with vested interests further their agenda, then you are deviating from your core objectives. Please do not let it happen," he said.toi news

World.title: '5,200 applications have been received' for CEO post: Ram Mandir Trust holds second meeting after donation row
World.content:
NEW DELHI: The Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Teerth Kshetra Trust on Wednesday held its second meeting in Ayodhya since the alleged donation embezzlement case surfaced, reviewing administrative matters as the probe continues.

The trust said it has received 5,200 applications for the post of CEO of the Ram Mandir, but has deferred the appointment by a month to allow the selection committee more time to scrutinise the applications. It also announced plans to set up a permanent institute to train and certify priests for the temple.

Addressing a press conference after the meeting, trust treasurer Govind Dev Giri said the trust had decided to establish a permanent institute for training priests.

"We have decided to set up a permanent institute for training priests, who would be certified by the Ram temple trust," Giri said.

He said the trust had received 5,200 applications for the CEO post.

"A total of 5,200 applications have been received for the Ram temple trust CEO post. Considering the volume of applications, the selection committee sought one month's additional time, which has been approved by the Trust," Giri said.





He added that the trust would appoint a secretary on an interim basis to meet its growing administrative requirements until the CEO is selected.

Interim general secretary Krishna Mohan said there was no discussion on appointing the CEO as the trust is still awaiting the report of the Special Investigation Team (SIT) probing the alleged donation embezzlement case.

"There was no discussion on the appointment of the CEO as the SIT report has not been received yet," Krishna Mohan said.

The trust also announced the formation of a permanent committee to oversee the religious affairs of the Ram temple.

According to Giri, the committee will comprise nine saints, including five from Ayodhya and four from outside, to supervise the temple's religious activities.

The meeting comes weeks after the trust accepted the resignations of its former general secretary Champat Rai and trustee Anil Mishra following the alleged donation embezzlement case. Krishna Mohan was appointed interim general secretary, while an SIT was constituted to investigate the allegations.

World.title: 'Unacceptable in a democratic society': SC bar bodies condemn police action against protesters, lawyers during CJP march
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Two Supreme Court bar bodies on Wednesday condemned the alleged police brutality against students and lawyers during the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP)-led July 20 march to Parliament, calling for an impartial inquiry into the "excessive use of force" and demanding accountability from those responsible.

The Supreme Court Bar Association (SCBA), headed by its president and senior advocate Vikas Singh, in a resolution, alleged that the police action left several students and members of the legal fraternity, including SCBA members, injured.

The resolution, issued by SCBA secretary Pragya Baghel, described the use of force against the protesters as "deeply disturbing and wholly unacceptable in a democratic society".

The bar body urged the authorities concerned to conduct an immediate, impartial and time-bound inquiry into the incident, identify those responsible for the alleged excessive use of force, and take appropriate action in accordance with the law.

It also called for proper medical treatment and assistance for all injured students and members of the legal fraternity, while urging authorities to take steps to prevent similar incidents in the future.





"The association stands in solidarity with all those injured and reiterates its commitment to protecting constitutional rights, human dignity and the rule of law," the resolution added.

In a separate statement, the Supreme Court Advocates-on-Record Association (SCAORA) expressed deep concern over "reports and visuals showing the use of force by Delhi Police against students and young protesters" who had gathered to peacefully raise concerns over the integrity of public examinations and the future of the country's youth.

SCAORA, in its resolution, maintained that peaceful dissent was not an act of defiance but an exercise of fundamental freedoms guaranteed under Articles 19(1)(a) and 19(1)(b) of the Constitution. It added that while the State has the authority to maintain public order, any restriction on these freedoms must meet the constitutional requirements of legality, necessity and proportionality.

The association called for an independent and impartial examination of allegations of excessive force, immediate medical assistance for those injured, and a more restrained, dialogue-based approach while engaging with peaceful protesters.

"The strength of our Republic lies not in suppressing dissent but in protecting it within the framework of the Constitution. The true measure of constitutional governance is not how the State responds to agreement, but how it responds to peaceful disagreement," the resolution added.

On Monday, thousands of students demanding the resignation of Union education minister Dharmendra Pradhan over the NEET paper leak issue and alleged irregularities in the examination system attempted to march to Parliament but were stopped by police using tear gas and batons.

World.title: 'Used to getting punched': Rahul Gandhi says he is 'ready to take many more' after detention during NEET protest
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Congress MP and Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi on Wednesday said he was âused to getting punchedâ and was ready to âtake many moreâ while standing with students protesting over the alleged NEET-UG 2026 paper leak and demanding reforms in the education system.

His remarks came a day after he, along with Congress leader Priyanka Gandhi Vadra, Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav and other opposition leaders was detained by Delhi Police during a sit-in outside Prime Minister Narendra Modi's residence over the issue.

Addressing a press conference at the AICC headquarters, Gandhi said standing up for students, farmers and young people was part of his responsibility as the Leader of the Opposition.

Responding to a question about his detention and the police action during Tuesday's protest, Gandhi said, "It's fine. I'm used to getting punched and all. It's no problem. My job is to express the will of India's people, whether it is the will of the students, whether it is the will of young people, whether it is the will of the farmers. This is the job that I am supposed to do as leader of opposition."

He added, "I am supposed to become an expression of the voice of India's people.





I am supposed to bring attention to where pain is being felt. These are very small costs. These are not big costs. It's a huge honour for me to do this, to be able to stand with the wishes of my people. So couple of punches and all. This is not a problem at all. I'm happy to take many more."

Replying to another question about what happened outside the Prime Minister's residence, Gandhi said, "My job is to express the will of India's people.

Whether it is the will of the students, the young people, or the farmers, this is the job I am supposed to do as the Leader of the Opposition. I am supposed to become an expression of the voice of India's people. I am supposed to bring attention to where pain is being felt. These are very small costs, not big ones.

It is a huge honour for me to do this, to be able to stand with the wishes of my people. So a couple of punches and all, that is not a problem at all.

I am happy to take many more."

During the press conference, Gandhi reiterated his criticism of the Centre over the alleged examination irregularities, accusing the government of destroying India's education system and expressing full support for the protesting students.

He said students were demanding a fair education system and backed their demand for the resignation of Union education minister Dharmendra Pradhan.

Gandhi also demanded that those responsible for the alleged police action against students be held accountable and said Prime Minister Narendra Modi should apologise to them.

He claimed that 152 paper leaks had taken place over the past decade with 'zero convictions', alleged that 7.5 crore students and their families had been affected, and said the country's education system had become "rigged" and unaffordable.

Rahul Gandhi's remarks came a day after he, Priyanka Gandhi Vadra, Akhilesh Yadav and several opposition leaders staged a sit-in outside Prime Minister Narendra Modi's residence, demanding a discussion on the alleged NEET paper leak, the resignation of education minister Dharmendra Pradhan and action over the police crackdown on students.

Delhi Police later removed and detained the leaders after the protest entered the high-security zone.

Rahul Gandhi was taken to Chhatrasal Stadium before being released a few hours later, while Priyanka Gandhi and some Congress MPs were taken to Mandir Marg police station and later released.

The Congress also released videos and photographs showing Rahul Gandhi and Priyanka Gandhi being removed by police during the protest.

One video showed Rahul Gandhi lying on the road as police personnel attempted to carry him away, while another appeared to show him being dragged during the detention.

The party also shared a photograph that appeared to show him with a nosebleed following the police action.

The Congress has accused the government of suppressing protests over the alleged examination irregularities, while the Centre has said it was willing to discuss the issue in Parliament and criticised the opposition's protest outside the PM Modi's residence.

World.title: Evening news wrap: Sonam Wangchuk sets condition for ending fast; Rahul Gandhi demands Dharmendra Pradhan's exit over NEET row & more
World.content:
Sonam Wangchuk to end fast only if protesters get legal immunity.

to end fast only if protesters get legal immunity. Rahul Gandhi demands Dharmendra Pradhan 's resignation over NEET row.

demands 's resignation over NEET row. Kalyan Banerjee suspended, calls rebel NCPI MPs "traitors".

Sensex, Nifty tumble as Iran tensions and Trump tariffs rattle markets.

US-Iran tensions deepen with fresh strikes, warnings and regional alerts.

Here are the top stories of the day:

Sonam Wangchuk says he'll end fast only after assurance for protesters

Climate activist Sonam Wangchuk has refused to end his hunger strike over the NEET paper leak until the Centre guarantees that no legal action will be taken against participants of the July 20 'Chalo Sansad' march.

In a letter to Union ministers JP Nadda and Jitendra Singh, Wangchuk said he wanted to return to teaching but would continue his fast unless the government assured protection for peaceful protesters and addressed key demands on accountability.

Rahul Gandhi demands Dharmendra Pradhan's exit over NEET row

Congress leader Rahul Gandhi accused the Centre of turning India's education system into a "rigged system" over the alleged NEET-UG paper leak and demanded education minister Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation.

Backing student protests, he alleged 152 paper leaks in the last decade with "zero convictions" and criticised police action against demonstrators.

Kalyan Banerjee suspended, calls rebel MPs 'traitors'

TMC MP Kalyan Banerjee was suspended from the Lok Sabha for the remainder of the Monsoon Session over alleged indecent and misogynistic remarks against women MPs during a heated exchange with rebel NCPI members. After the suspension, Banerjee called the rebel MPs "traitors" and claimed they lacked public support in West Bengal.





Sensex, Nifty slide as global risks spook markets

Equity markets fell sharply, with the Sensex shedding 715 points and the Nifty slipping below 24,000 as escalating US-Iran tensions, surging crude oil prices and fresh tariff threats from US President Donald Trump dampened investor sentiment. Pharma stocks led the losses after Trump's proposed tariffs on imported generic medicines, while a weaker rupee and rising US Treasury yields added to the market pressure, wiping out nearly Rs 4.25 lakh crore in investor wealth.

US-Iran tensions escalate amid strikes, regional alerts

The US and Iran exchanged fresh warnings as secretary of state Marco Rubio said Washington remained open to diplomacy but would not tolerate threats to commercial shipping or the Strait of Hormuz. Iran claimed to have targeted military bases in Jordan, while reports also emerged of explosions in southern Iran and an alleged US strike on Larak Island. Bahrain and Saudi Arabia activated emergency alerts as regional tensions continued to intensify.

World.title: Politics of silence: Is NCP(SP) chief Sharad Pawar keeping options open on Delimitation Bill?
World.content:
Pressure to keep his flock together

The balancing act

On July 7, Maharashtra chief minister and senior BJP leader Devendra Fadnavis announced that no new party will be joining the National Democratic Alliance (NDA) or the state's Mahayuti alliance at present.

On July 8, Sharad Pawar paid a courtesy visit to Maharashtra deputy chief minister Eknath Shinde at the Vidhan Bhavan complex. Pawar also met his party MLAs at Shindeâs office.

On July 12, NCP (SP) leader Eknath Khadse, currently a member of the legislative council (MLC), acknowledged that he had travelled to Delhi and had met BJP general secretary Vinod Tawde. Khadse claimed that Amit Shah had called him and asked him to join the BJP.

World.title: Police freeze ₹10 lakh of ₹19.8 lakh lost by Mangaluru resident
World.content:
The Mangaluru Cyber, Economic offenses, and Narcotics (CEN) police froze ₹10 lakh of the ₹19.8 lakh allegedly lost by a Mangaluru resident in an online investment fraud.

In a complaint to the CEN police, a 53-year-old resident of Derebail said a woman identifying herself as Ananya Kulkarni sent him a WhatsApp link to what she claimed was Finsol Sarathi Plan, promising high returns on investment. The complainant clicked on the link and opened an account and transferred ₹19.8 lakh between June 29 and July 20 as investments. When the complainant sought to withdraw the amount, the woman reportedly asked him to invest more money. Suspecting fraud, the victim approached the police and filed a complaint.

Soon after registration of the case, the CEN police tracked the money trail and took action to freeze ₹10 lakh of the ₹19.8 lakh invested by the victim.

Commissioner of Police (CP) Sudheer Kumar Reddy said police would return the amount to the victim after obtaining a court permission, while continuing the search for the fraudster. Mr. Reddy called upon victims to approach police at the earliest, as this would help police take measures to recover money lost to fraudsters.

World.title: Doctor in Kerala’s Kannur booked over alleged medical negligence, hospital denies charges
World.content:
The Kannur Town police have registered a case against a doctor at KIMS Sreechand Hospital after a patient alleged that she was discharged without the fish bone lodged in her throat being removed, resulting in prolonged pain and further surgery.

The case was been registered against Dr. Gaurav Baber, 35, following a complaint by P.V. Savithri, a resident of Echikkovil, Pilicode, in Kasaragod district.

In the complaint, Ms. Savithri said she was admitted to the hospital after a fish bone got stuck in her throat. Following an endoscopic procedure, doctors told her that the bone had been removed, and that she had been discharged. However, her throat pain persisted. Further treatment and a CT scan at the Pariyaram Government Medical College Hospital (MCH) revealed that another fish bone remained lodged in her throat. The retained bone was later surgically removed at the hospital.

The police said the case was registered after a preliminary inquiry into a complaint submitted by Ms. Savithiri to the Deputy Inspector General of Police, Kannur, alleging medical negligence and physical suffering caused by the treatment.

Responding to the allegations, the KIMS Sreechand Hospital authorities denied any medical negligence and said the incident had occured in February this year. According to the hospital, the patient underwent an endoscopic removal of the fish bone after an X-ray identified a foreign body in her throat.

The hospital said the treating gastroenterologist had advised a CT scan after the procedure, in line with the standard protocol, to confirm that no additional foreign body remained in the patient’s throat. However, the patient allegedly declined to undergo the scan citing financial constraints and took discharge against the doctor’s advice. She was also asked to return for review after two days.

Instead, the patient later sought treatment at the Kannur Government MCH, where a CT scan reportedly detected another fish bone, which was subsequently removed, said hospital administrator Muhammed Nabeel.

KIMS hospital maintained that no surgery was performed at the hospital, contrary to the complaint, and that only an endoscopic procedure had been done. The hospital said all procedures and medical records were fully documented, and that it had cooperated with the police investigation.

According to the hospital, the police had earlier heard the doctor’s explanation during the preliminary inquiry, and the management believes that the case is without merit. It alleged that the complaint was intended to tarnish the reputation of the hospital.

World.title: ABVP seeks panel for reforms in competitive examinations
World.content:
The Akhil Bharatiya Vidyarthi Parishad (ABVP) has urged the Union government to constitute a high-level committee to enhance transparency and undertake institutional reforms in competitive examinations, including NEET-UG.

In a statement issued on Wednesday, ABVP State secretary Y. Venkata Gopi said students should not become instruments of narrow political interests or anti-national forces. He said the organisation strongly condemned the unrest and clashes that occurred during the protest at Jantar Mantar over NEET-UG and other education-related issues.

Expressing concern over the confrontations between some protesters, who identified themselves as students, and security personnel, Mr. Gopi said such incidents had disturbed public order in Delhi. He alleged that certain politically motivated individuals and anti-social elements had attempted to exploit the genuine concerns of students and turn the protest into a platform for violence.

Mr. Gopi expressed sympathy for the students and security personnel injured in the clashes and hoped such incidents would not recur.

He said the ABVP had, from the outset, demanded action against irregularities in competitive examinations, including a re-conduct of NEET-UG wherever warranted. The organisation had also consistently sought a Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) inquiry into the alleged examination irregularities to safeguard the credibility and transparency of the examination system. It had also staged protests in front of the National Testing Agency (NTA) headquarters, demanding strict action against those responsible.

World.title: Mamata loyalist Kunal Ghosh marshalled out of West Bengal Assembly after he disrupts dissident MLA’s speech
World.content:
Trinamool Congress MLA Kunal Ghosh was on Wednesday (July 22, 2026) marshalled out of the West Bengal Assembly for disrupting the speech of Opposition Chief Whip Akhruzzaman.

Mr. Ghosh, a Mamata Banerjee loyalist, was upset at not being allowed to speak during the discussion on the Home Department’s budget. Mr. Akhruzaman belongs to the dissident camp of the Trinamool Congress led by Leader of the Opposition Ritabrata Banerjee.

Dispute between the two rival groups of the Trinamool Congress was brewing over the past two days over who would be given priority in speaking in the House during discussions. Mr. Ghosh and other Mamata loyalists have been claiming that Mr. Akhruzzaman has been striking out the names of MLAs who are loyalist to Ms. Banerjee to participate in discussions in the Assembly.

Also Read | Loyalists rally behind Mamata, say an ousted leader cannot lead Trinamool in Assembly

During the proceedings in the Assembly on Wednesday, when Mr. Akhruzzaman started discussion on the Budget of the Home Department, Mr. Ghosh went in front of his seat and interrupted: “Why are you crossing out my name [in the list of speakers]?”

While Mr. Akhruzzaman continued his speech, Mr. Ghosh continued to question him. Minister for Parliamentary Affairs Shankar Ghosh and Higher Education Minister Jagannath Chatterjee tried to intervene. Speaker Rathindra Basu requested Mr. Ghosh to return to his seat. When Mr. Ghosh did not move, the Speaker warned him “Kunalbabu, if you do not return to your seat, I will be forced to throw you out”.

Noisy protests

Mr. Ghosh resisted eviction, prompting Assembly marshals to lift and carry him out of the House after repeated appeals by the Speaker failed to restore order. The scuffle triggered noisy protests, with members descending into the well of the House before proceedings could resume. The developments in the Assembly came a day after the Mamata Banerjee loyalists and dissidents in the Ritabrata Banerjee camp held public meetings in Kolkata targeting each other.

The Speaker subsequently suspended Mr. Ghosh from the House for the remainder of the day. Industries Minister Tapas Roy initially demanded that Mr. Ghosh be suspended for the rest of the ongoing Assembly session till Saturday, citing his “unruly behaviour”. Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari, however, intervened, saying there was no need to “make him a hero” by suspending him for the entire session and suggested that a suspension for the day would suffice. The Chief Minister expressed his displeasure over the developments and said he was Leader of the Opposition and never witnessed such a behaviour.

Speaking to media persons later in the day, Mr. Ghosh said the BJP in West Bengal wanted to control the Opposition. “They [BJP government] are not willing to listen to any criticism. Even in the past I was not allowed to speak when Sobhandeb Chattopadhyay [leader of Mamata loyalist group] had nominated me,” he said.

Mr. Ghosh said the MLAs of the dissident group of Trinamool Congress did not criticise the BJP government and were being promoted by the BJP government.

World.title: Pidari Ekaveeri: a fierce Goddess, a captivating smile, and Raja Raja’s mother-in-law’s grant
World.content:
Within the precincts of the ancient Sadaimudinathar Temple at Tiruvalanchuzhi, near Kumbakonam, stands a remarkable image of Pidari Ekaveeri, a deity whose significance is illuminated by the temple’s inscriptions. The temple, celebrated in the hymns of the Shaivite saints and renowned as an architectural marvel of the Chola period, is also home to inscriptions that reveal an equally fascinating chapter in its religious history.

According to the inscriptions, the endowment for the worship of Pidari Ekaveeri was made by Kunthanan Amuthavalliyar, the mother of Queen Thanthisathi Vidankiyar and the mother-in-law of the Chola emperor Raja Raja I. The inscription records that she donated 40 gold coins to six Brahmins — Thalaisenan Valanchuzhian, Ezhuvan Thalaisenan, Sathan Patta Somasi, Patta Somasi Selvan, Aramudhu Tiruvikraman, and Nakkan Pandithan — for conducting Avapala Anjanai, a special ritual of worship.

R. Kalaikovan of the Dr. Rajamanickanar Centre for Historical Research, who identified the dilapidated shrine hidden underneath dense vegetation within the Tiruvalanchuzhi temple complex and studied its inscriptions, said the annual interest from this endowment amounted to 30 kalam of paddy. This income was earmarked for performing the Avapala Anjanai, during which food and betel were offered to the deity while a perpetual lamp was kept burning.

Dr. Kalaikovan further noted that when temple endowments were resettled during the reign of Rajendra II, an annual allocation of 15 kalam of paddy continued to be earmarked for the worship of Pidari Ekaveeri, demonstrating the continuity of the cult across successive Chola reigns.

Today, Pidari Ekaveeri is identified as Ashtapuja Durgai, because she is depicted with eight arms and now stands outside the sanctum of the Vandarkuzhali shrine.

Originally, the deity was inside the dilapidated shrine. After that shrine collapsed, the image was relocated to its present position. The overgrown remnants of the old shrine, still concealed beneath thorny bushes within the temple complex, silently testifies to its forgotten past.

Chola artistry

The sculpture itself is a masterpiece of Chola artistry. The goddess is seated gracefully in utkuti asana, her face adorned with a serene and captivating smile that contrasts strikingly with her fierce iconographic features. Her matted locks spread majestically, crowned by a skull embraced by two serpents. An owl forms the ornament of her right ear, while a tiny human figure hangs from her left ear as an earring. Across her torso she wears a garland of skulls in place of the sacred thread, combining beauty, power, and esoteric symbolism into a single compelling image.

Dr. Kalaikovan pointed out that although several inscriptions from the Chola period refer to Pidari deities, the corresponding images have rarely been identified. “Even in temples where Pidari images survive, there are no inscriptions to establish their antiquity. At Tiruvalanchuzhi, however, we are able to directly connect the inscriptions with the deity still enshrined in the temple. Pidari Ekaveeri is probably the oldest identifiable Pidari image in Tamil Nadu,” he said.

The image of Pidari Ekaveeri is therefore much more than an exquisite work of Chola sculpture. Together with the inscriptions documenting its royal patronage and ritual traditions, it stands as an invaluable historical record, preserving one of the earliest identifiable traditions of Pidari worship in Tamil Nadu and offering a rare window into the religious life of the Chola age.

World.title: UAE, Saudi officials signal rapprochement after rift
World.content:
Top officials and Ministers in the United Arab Emirates and Saudi Arabia have recently posted about friendship and unity on social media, signalling a rapprochement months after a public fall-out between the two largest Arab economies.

On Tuesday (July 21) evening, Saudi General Entertainment Authority chairman Turki Alalshikh posted a picture of the kingdom's defence minister Khaled bin Salman, alongside Emirati Vice President Mansour bin Zayed, that he said was taken a few days ago.

"Saudi Arabia and the UAE: A story of brotherly relations and a strong partnership," he wrote in his post on X.

UAE presidential advisor Anwar Gargash also shared the picture, with the caption: "The biggest story in the Gulf is captured in a single photograph."

For months, pundits from both sides had engaged in virulent debate online, with Saudi Arabia also launching earlier this year a media campaign against its smaller neighbour.

The two allies-turned-rivals had a public falling out in December when the kingdom accused Abu Dhabi of threatening its national security by supporting Yemeni separatists who orchestrated a brief offensive.

The pair have been at odds in their foreign policy from Yemen and Sudan to the Horn of Africa, where they have supported rival forces.

Their differences have spilt over into the Iran conflict, with the kingdom backing Pakistani mediation efforts, while the UAE initially took a more hawkish stance on Tehran, prior to the signing of a U.S.-Iran memorandum of understanding last month.

The apparent mending of ties came as U.S.-Iran hostilities resumed this month, triggering renewed Iranian attacks across the Gulf, while Tehran's Houthi allies in Yemen ramped up the pressure by threatening a naval blockade of the kingdom.

UAE Chairman of the National Media Authority Abdulla Alhamed and Saudi Media Minister Salman Aldosary posted very similar messages on X on Tuesday (July 21), lauding relations between the two countries and their leaders, while stating that "responsible media" must reflect this bond.

"The role of responsible media is to counter anyone attempting to portray a misleading image of the relationship between the two countries and to ensure accuracy in all published information," Mr. Aldosary said in his post, praising the "wise leadership in both countries".

World.title: KPCL steps up thermal power generation to ensure reliable power supply across Karnataka
World.content:
The Karnataka Power Corporation Limited (KPCL) has stepped up thermal power generation to ensure adequate and reliable electricity supply across the State amid declining reservoir levels and hydropower generation due to deficient rainfall.

As part of its efforts to meet the State’s power requirements, the KPCL has been generating an average of 84.34 million units of thermal power every day in July. The corporation is maintaining its thermal power plants in optimal operating condition and taking measures to further augment generation, with a target of increasing daily thermal power output to 100 million units in the coming days, said a release.

Energy and Tourism Minister K.J. George has already reviewed the KPCL’s power generation activities and directed officials to take necessary measures to ensure that power generation is in line with demand.

Increased thermal power generation

During this monsoon, particularly in July, there has been a significant increase in both coal supplies and power generation at the three thermal power plants in the State. During July last year, the average daily generation stood at 54.47 million units as against the average of 84.34 million units of thermal power this year.

At the Raichur Thermal Power Station, an average of 24.45 million units of electricity is being generated per day in July this year, compared to an average of 13.12 million units per day during July last year.

At the Ballari Thermal Power Station, an average of 33.64 million units of electricity is being generated per day, compared to 25.35 million units per day during July last year.

At the Yermarus Thermal Power Station, an average of 26.25 million units of electricity is being generated per day, compared to 16 million units per day during July last year, the release said.

Increase in coal stock

Measures have already been taken to increase coal stocks to facilitate higher power generation at thermal power plants. During the corresponding period last year, coal stocks were sufficient for 12 days of generation. This year, stocks sufficient for 15 days have been maintained. Steps are also being taken to increase coal stocks to a level sufficient for 20 days of operation. To achieve this, arrangements have been made to receive 17–18 coal rakes per day, said the release.

World.title: Early return of cattle proposed as tiger attacks rise in plantations
World.content:
Amid recurring tiger attacks on cattle in the tea plantation areas of Devikulam and Munnar, the Forest department plans to direct plantation managements to ensure that livestock are brought into sheds early in the afternoon.

Tigers have been regularly preying on cattle across both forest ranges. According to Forest department officials, 34 cattle have been attacked under the Devikulam range in the past six months. However, plantation workers claim the real figure is close to 200 over the past year in both ranges.

Preventing overnight grazing

Officials noted that workers often leave cattle in the tea estates to graze, with many remaining there overnight. “Easy prey availability has led to tigers camping in the tea plantations,” a senior forest official said. “The Forest department has repeatedly asked plantation companies to limit cattle numbers and prevent overnight grazing, but these requests have not yet been addressed.” said the official.

Devikulam Range Officer E.D. Arunkumar confirmed the growing severity of the situation. “Allowing cattle in tea plantations at night attracts tigers,” Arunkumar said. “If we stop leaving cattle out overnight, we can significantly reduce these attacks. The department will ask plantation management to ensure cattle are brought back to the shed by 3 p.m. Bringing them in early also allows workers to identify missing livestock right away. Without support from estate managements, the department cannot resolve this issue,” he added.

According to officials, the unchecked growth of the cattle population on estates is the primary driver of the problem. Workers typically bring only milking cows into sheds at night, leaving the other cattle exposed in the fields. “The tigers find easy prey here,” the senior official said. “Another concern is that because prey is so easy to catch in these estates, tigers in Munnar and Devikulam lose the instinct to hunt wild prey.”

This behaviour was highlighted in April, when a tiger captured in Munnar after repeated attacks was relocated to Gavi in the Periyar Tiger Reserve (PTR). Within days, the big cat strayed into a tea plantation in Vandiperiyar to hunt cattle again. “The department has been making extensive efforts to capture or tranquilise the animal over the past two months, but it continues to evade search teams,” the official added.

World.title: We all need our moments of quiet but how do you shape one within your home?
World.content:
The Home Edit is a weekly series curated by Shiny Varghese that invites architects and designers to share their hands-on expertise on ideas for your home. Whether you are building, renovating, or simply refreshing a space, the series provides actionable advice and inspiration to help you make better choices for where you live. In this part of the series, Kapil Aggarwal shares tips for designing a sacred corner.

A home temple or altar is more than a designated place for prayer, it is a space for reflection, gratitude and everyday rituals. Whether integrated into a compact apartment or a larger residence, a thoughtfully designed sacred corner can bring a sense of calm and purpose to daily life. Here are a few practical dos and don’ts to consider when planning one.

1. Choose the Right Location

Do: Select a quiet and relatively undisturbed area of the home where you can sit comfortably for prayer or meditation. Natural light can enhance the experience and create a sense of openness.

Don’t: Place the temple in high-traffic zones, directly adjacent to entertainment units, or in spaces that are primarily used for storage. A sacred space should feel intentional rather than incidental.

2. Prioritise Simplicity and Proportion

Do: Design the altar in proportion to the available space. A compact niche, wall-mounted unit, or dedicated room can all work equally well when planned thoughtfully.

Don’t: Overcrowd the area with excessive decorative elements, large idols in a limited space, or too many objects that make maintenance difficult. Simplicity often allows the spiritual significance of the space to stand out.

Allow the space to reflect your family’s traditions and practices (Photo: Spaces Architects@KA) Allow the space to reflect your family’s traditions and practices (Photo: Spaces Architects@KA)

3. Pay Attention to Materials and Lighting

Do: Use durable, easy-to-maintain materials such as wood, stone, metal or laminate finishes. Layered lighting, including concealed lights or soft accent illumination, can create a serene atmosphere.



Don’t: Use harsh lighting or highly reflective finishes that create visual clutter. The focus should remain on the altar rather than on decorative effects.

4. Ensure Practical Functionality

Do: Incorporate storage for prayer books, incense, diyas, and other essentials. Proper ventilation is also important, particularly if incense or lamps are used regularly.

Don’t: Ignore practical needs in favour of aesthetics. A beautiful temple that is difficult to use or maintain will eventually lose its purpose.

5. Make It Personal

Do: Allow the space to reflect your family’s traditions and practices. Artwork, handcrafted elements, or meaningful heirlooms can add depth and authenticity.



Don’t: Replicate designs solely because they are trending. A home temple is most meaningful when it reflects personal beliefs and daily rituals rather than a catalogue image.

ALSO READ | Paintings are not the only way to bring art into your home

6. Prioritise Fire Safety

Do: Place diyas and candles on stable stone, metal, or ceramic surfaces, and keep them away from curtains, fabrics, and decorative items. If soft furnishings are used near the temple, opt for fire-retardant or fire-resistant materials wherever possible. Ensure adequate ventilation, especially in built-in temple units. Make it a habit to extinguish flames before leaving the house or retiring for the night. For longer periods of illumination, enclosed lamps or LED alternatives can be a safer choice.

Don’t: Leave burning diyas or candles unattended, especially in enclosed niches, beneath overhead shelves, or near fabrics and decorative elements. Avoid placing oil lamps where they can be accidentally knocked over by children, pets, or passing movement.

Kapil Aggarwal is principal architect, Spaces Architects@KA. His works include the UNESCO-awarded restoration of Haveli Dharampura in Old Delhi

World.title: Kuldeep Yadav joins Yorkshire for County matches, One-Day Cup
World.content:
India spinner Kuldeep Yadav has joined English County side Yorkshire to play five one-day matches and three red-ball games, the club said on Wednesday. Kuldeep will play the One-Day Cup games from July 24 to August 2 before joining India for their two-Test tour of Sri Lanka in August. He will then rejoin Yorkshire for playing their final three County Championship matches of the season.



“I’m really pleased to be joining Yorkshire and grateful for this opportunity,” said Kuldeep. “It will be a real privilege to represent a Club with Yorkshire’s proud history. I’ve always enjoyed the challenge of playing in English conditions and after speaking with the management, I became really excited to join up with the team and I’m looking forward to making a positive contribution during my time at Headingley.”

World.title: Police use water cannons as BJP, Congress hold rival protests in Jaipur
World.content:
Tense confrontations with police marked counter-protests by the Congress and the BJP in Jaipur on Wednesday, as authorities used water cannons to stop the marchers in a spillover of the previous day’s NEET demonstrations in the national capital.

The BJP, led by state president Madan Rathore, marched from the party office towards the Congress headquarters to protest the rival party’s Tuesday demonstration outside Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s residence. The march was halted by police barricades at Chomu House. As the protesters tried to cross the barricades, a scuffle broke out with the police, prompting them to use water cannons.



After the protest, Rathore, drenched in the police action, accused the demonstrators at Jantar Mantar of being “hired agitators and trained stone-pelters” in a protest “funded from abroad”.

World.title: Amid Ken-Betwa uproar, Madhya Pradesh government promises inquiry
World.content:
The Madhya Pradesh government on Tuesday said there would be an inquiry into complaints surrounding the rehabilitation of families displaced by the Rs 44,605-crore Ken-Betwa Link Project, after Leader of Opposition Umang Singhar alleged large-scale irregularities in compensation, rehabilitation surveys and Gram Sabha proceedings during a heated exchange in the Assembly.

Replying to Singhar’s questions, Revenue Minister Karan Singh Verma maintained that almost all affected families had been compensated under the rehabilitation package and denied any scam. However, Chief Minister Mohan Yadav intervened to assure the House that any complaint brought before the government would be investigated and promised to complete the exercise within a month.
